1N3B: Chugai = pecks (food). Chitaarai = remembers (her young). Bhee = again, then. Chug chug chitaare = pecking and pecking (she remembers her young; she both pecks food and remembers her young).
O Kabir! The crane pecks her food and also remembers her young; again she pecks, both pecking food and remembering her young.
Kabeer, the flamingo pecks and feeds, and remembers her chicks.
Kabir, the flamingo pecks, at her feet and remembers her offspring. As she pecks and pecks, she again remembers her offspring.
Sri Kabir ji says: just as the crane, pecking grain, remembers her young, and again, pecking and pecking, remembers them —
3UEU: Bacharahi = in the young. Mamta = the thought that (Maya) may become mine, longing for ownership. Re = O brother! ||123||
Just as the crane's attention stays always on her young, so (when 'Hari's remembrance is given up') a person's mind stays fixed in the longing to own Maya. ||123||
She pecks and pecks and feeds, and remembers them always. Her chicks are very dear to her, just like the love of wealth and Maya is dear to the mortal's mind. ||123||
As the offspring are dear to the flamingo so is the love of wealth to your mind, O man.
just as the young dwell in the crane's mind, (re) O brother, so too this being is gripped by possessiveness for Maya. ||123||
XUT2: Ambar = sky, heavens. Ghanhar = cloud. Chhaaia = spread, covered. Barakh = raining. Sar taal = pools and ponds.
O Kabir! (In the rainy season) the cloud spreads (all round) the sky and, raining, fills (all the small and great) pools and ponds,
Kabeer, the sky is overcast and cloudy; the ponds and lakes are overflowing with water.
Kabir, the sky is overcast with clouds and the lakes and tanks are filled with the rain-water.

Sri Kabir ji says: in the sky that is Braham, the cloud that is the True Guru is settled, and, raining the water of teaching, fills the ponds, unbaked and baked, that are seekers excellent and middling.
GWEF: Chaatrik = rain-bird. Rahai = rahain, remain. Kaun havaal = (that is) only a bad state. ||124||

(but the rain-bird still keeps longing and crying for a drop of rain. Parmatma pervades all creation, but beings caught in possessiveness over Maya cannot see Him;) ('giving up Hari's remembrance') they plead like the rain-bird, and their state is always wretched. ||124||
Like the rainbird, some remain thirsty - what is their condition? ||124||
They, who remain thirsty like the pied cuckoo; what would their condition be?
While such a rain of teaching falls, the beings who stay longing like the rain-bird — meaning, who do not take up devotion — what will their state be? That is, only wretched. ||124||
2L09: Chakaee = the chakvi bird (Note: it is commonly believed that the chakvi stays separated from her mate the chakva all night. They cry out in memory of each other but cannot meet; as soon as morning comes they meet again). Jau = when. Nis = at night. Parbhaat = before sunrise.

O Kabir! When the chakvi is separated (from her chakva) at night, she comes and meets him again at dawn (the darkness of night is an obstacle to their meeting, but this darkness can separate them for four watches at most;
Kabeer, the chakvi duck is separated from her love through the night, but in the morning, she meets him again.
Kabir, the sheldrake, which is separated for the night from her love, comes and meets him in the morning.
Sri Kabir ji says: just as the chakvi is separated from the chakva at night, and at dawn comes back to meet her master the chakva —
0XTM: but the darkness of possessiveness over Maya is not such as ends soon; it does not let go through birth after birth; because of this darkness) the people who are separated from Prabhu meet Him neither by day nor by night. ||125||
Those who are separated from the Lord do not meet Him in the day, or in the night. ||125||
The men, who are separated from the Lord, meet Him neither in the day nor in the night.
but the people separated from Ram — that is, who have become self-willed — never meet again, by day or by night; meaning, they stay always separated from Ram. ||125||
QLTF: Rainaair = (Sanskrit ratnaakar, the mine of jewels) the ocean. Majhoor = (rainaair) maajh, right in the ocean. Rahu = stay.
O Kabir! O conch separated from the ocean! Stay right in the ocean,
Kabeer: O conch shell, remain in the ocean.
Kabir, O conch, remain you in the ocean; separating from it,
Sri Kabir ji says: O conch that is the being! You have separated your mind from the (rainaair) ocean that is Parmatma; so stay (majhoor) within that ocean.
9Z7M: Deval = (devaalaya, dev-aalaya) the house of a god, shrine, temple. Dhaahrree = dhaah-rree, a terrible wail. Desahi = you will give. Soor = sun. ||126||
otherwise every day at sunrise you will give a terrible wail in every temple. ||126||
If you are separated from it, you shall scream at sunrise from temple to temple. ||126||
otherwise, you shall have to give out scream at sun rise at every temple.
Otherwise, at the rising of the sun of death you will go wailing from temple to temple of bodies; meaning, taking births you will stay in pain. ||126||
EYGR: Soota = asleep (in the sleep of possessiveness over Maya). Bhai = (the world's) fears and dreads. Roe bhai dukh = (Note: see salok 72) remove the fears, dreads and pains of the world. (Note: to weep for someone means to break off one's bond with them.)

O Kabir! Asleep (drunk on attachment to Maya), what are you doing (why are you wasting your life)? Wake up in Prabhu's remembrance, and (through the blessing of this remembrance) gain release from the (worldly) fears and troubles (that surround one separated from Prabhu's feet). (You think the sleep of attachment is a sweet sleep, but staying pressed under the pains, troubles and fears born of attachment is like lying in a grave. This life full of pains, troubles and fears is no happy life.)
Kabeer, what are you doing sleeping? Wake up and cry in fear and pain.
Kabir what do you do by sleeping? Wakeup and weep over the fear and pain of death.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, what are you doing, asleep? Remembering the pains through the fear of the world, wake up and weep.
348H: Baasa = dwelling. Gor = grave, a dark deep place, a life full of the world's pains and fears. Kiu = how? Kiu sovai sukh = cannot sleep in peace, cannot be happy. ||127||
The person whose dwelling stays always in (such a) grave can never be said to live a happy life. ||127||
Those who live in the grave - how can they sleep in peace? ||127||
They, whose abode is in the grave, how can they sleep in peace?
The one whose dwelling is to be in the (gor) grave or tomb — how can they sleep happily? That is, they should stay awake and worship. ||127||
Y2KU: Uth = becoming alert, waking up. Ki = why? Muraar = Parmatma.
O Kabir! Drunk on attachment to Maya, why are you wasting your life? Waking up from this sleep of attachment, why do you not remember Parmatma?
Kabeer, what are you doing sleeping? Why not rise up and meditate on the Lord?
Kabir, what does you do by sleeping. Why wakeup and contemplate on God, the enemy of ego?
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, what are you doing, asleep? Why do you not get up and chant Muraari's Name?
M9R7: Pasaar = stretching out. Laanbe god pasaar = stretching out the knees long — so carefree that one will never get up again. ||128||
One day you will have to sleep so helpless that you will never be able to get up again (one day you will have to sleep the sleep that lasts for ever). ||128||
One day you shall sleep with your legs outstretched. ||128||
One day you shall sleep, stretching out yours knees at full-length.
For one day you will sleep with your knees stretched out long; meaning, one day the body will die. ||128||
UVRM: O Kabir! Drunk on attachment to Maya, why are you wasting your life? Be alert; stay watchful against the drowsy pull of the sleep of possessiveness.
Kabeer, what are you doing sleeping? Wake up, and sit up.
Kabir, what does you do by sleeping? You wakeup and keep sitting.
Sri Kabir ji says: so, O being, what will you do asleep? Sit up, and stay awake in chanting Vahiguru's Name.
KZRN: Ja ke sang te = from the company of the Parmatma. Laag = stay attached, stay joined. ||129||
Stay joined to the feet of that same Prabhu from whose remembrance you are separated (and so are bearing these fears and troubles). ||129||
Attach yourself to the One, from whom you have been separated. ||129||
He from whose company you are separated, to Him attach you yourself.
The Parmeshvar from whose company you are separated — attach yourself to Him alone; meaning, become one with Him. ||129||
ABFB: Gail = path, following. Sant kee gail = the path the saints walk. Maarag = on the path. Laaga jaau = keep walking.

(But) O Kabir! (If you want to make the effort of 'attaching yourself to the One from whom you are separated', then) do not leave the path the saints and Gurmukhs walk; one should keep walking on their path.
Kabeer, do not leave the Society of the Saints; walk upon this Path.
Kabir, leave you not the association of the saint and walk you on his path.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, do not leave (gail) following the saint; keep going on their path.
6YXG: Puneet = puneet, pure. Bhettat = by meeting, by keeping company, by sitting near. ||130||
By seeing the saints and Gurmukhs the mind becomes pure; by sitting near them one remembers Parmatma's Name (a love for remembrance arises). ||130||
See them, and be sanctified; meet them, and chant the Name. ||130||
Seeing him you shall be purified and meeting with him, you shall begin to recite the Lord's Name.
For by seeing them one becomes pure, and by (bhettat) meeting them one chants Vahiguru's Name. ||130||
Z2U4: Saakat = a person cut off from God. Sang = company. Doorahi = far (from the saakat). Bhaag jaaeeai = one should run away.

O Kabir! (If you want to make the effort of 'attaching yourself to the One from whom you are separated', then) one should not keep the company of a person cut off from God; one should keep far away from them.
Kabeer, do not associate with the faithless cynics; run far away from them.
Kabir, associate you not with the infidel and flee far away from him.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, do not keep the company of saakats; run far away from them.
4UC7: Baasan = vessel. Kaaro = black. Tau = then. Kachh = some, more or less. ||131||
(See:) if we touch a black vessel, some stain is bound to rub off. ||131||
If you touch a vessel stained with soot, some of the soot will stick to you. ||131||
If you touch a black vessel, then, some blot must attach to you.
For when you touch a black vessel, some stain will rub off; meaning, in the same way the company of saakats will only bring blemish. ||131||
1EBG: O Kabir! (If you want to make the effort of 'attaching yourself to the One from whom you are separated', it can only be done in good time; normally this effort should be made before old age. But if) in youth one did not remember Parmatma, (then) old age has arrived (and with attachment to Maya up to this age, countless bad impressions have piled up within; how will they let one turn to remembrance now?).
Kabeer, you have not contemplated the Lord, and now old age has overtaken you.
Kabir, you have not contemplated your Lord and the old age has come upon you.
Sri Kabir ji says: O being! You have not remembered Ram's Name, and now (jara) old age has come upon you.
DWJC: Laagee = (fire) has caught. Mandar = house. Mandar duaar te = from the door of the house. Ab = now, when the fire has caught. Kia kaadhia jaai = what can be saved? Not everything can be saved. ||132||

If a house catches fire from the doorway itself, then not much can be saved (from burning) (in the same way, if youth is rotted away in vices, then in old age, with the days of life numbered, life cannot be mended much). ||132||
Now that the door of your mansion is on fire, what can you take out? ||132||
Now when the door of your mansion is on fire; what can be taken out?

So when the fire of death has caught at the very door of the temple of the body, wise people say: O brother, what can be got out of it now? Meaning, when speech itself has stopped, when can the Name be chanted then? ||132||
RYP4: Kaaran = cause, means, the means of 'remembering Ram'. So bhaio = that alone (becomes the cause).

(But) O Kabir! (If youth has passed in straying from remembrance and understanding has come now that old age has arrived, still there is no need to despair. Remembrance is Prabhu's own gift; only when He gives it can the being remember. Whether youth or old age, the) cause (of remembrance) is only what the Creator Himself makes;
Kabeer, the Creator does whatever He pleases.
Kabir, the work, which the Creator does, that alone is accomplished.
Sri Kabir ji says: that alone has become the cause which the Creator has made.
SU6K: (this gift is in no being's hands; the One who makes this cause) is no other than that Parmatma; only the Creator of creation Himself is able to make this cause. ||133||
There is none other than Him; He alone is the Creator of all. ||133||
Without Him there is not another. He alone is the Creator of all.
For, other than that One Creator, there is no one else capable. ||133||
HGAM: Phal phalan laage = fruit begins to come on the mango trees, the mangoes begin to bear fruit.
O Kabir! The mango trees (first) bear fruit, and then (slowly) the fruit begins to ripen;
Kabeer, the fruit trees are bearing fruit, and the mangoes are becoming ripe.
Kabir, when the fruit trees being to bear fruit and the mangos begin to ripe.
Sri Kabir ji says: O being! The middling seekers have begun to bear the fruit of spiritual practices, and the excellent seekers too have begun to ripen through practices.
CV20: Khasam kau = to the master of the orchard. Jau = if. Beech = midway, before ripening. Kaanb = shaking, the fruit being shaken loose from the branch by storms and the like. ||134||
only if these mangoes are not shaken (loose from the branch by storms and the like) before ripening do they reach the master. ||134||
They will reach the owner, only if the crows do not eat them first. ||134||
They reach the owner, if the crows eat them not in the meantime.
If the (kaanb) taint of the vices of lust, anger and the rest, or of Maya, does not eat those seeker-fruits midway, then they go and reach the Master. ||134||
DZ90: Mol le = buying, purchasing. Jaahi = go.
O Kabir! The people who buy (an idol of) the Thakur and worship (it), and go to pilgrimage places out of stubbornness of mind,
Kabeer, some buy idols and worship them; in their stubborn-mindedness, they make pilgrimages to sacred shrines.
Kabir, men purchase and worship the god-idol and through their mind's obstinacy go on pilgrimage.
Sri Kabir ji says: the people who buy a Thakur and worship it, and go to pilgrimage places out of stubbornness of mind — meaning, who are empty of faith and conviction —
Y0RZ: Dekha dekhee = seeing one another (doing this). Saang dhar = putting on a show, imitating. Bhattka khaahi = wander. ||135||

(in truth those people) keep putting on a show, seeing one another (do this) (there is no reality in it; everything is done only to be called good among people; there is no surge of love for Parmatma in the heart; these people, strayed from the right path, wander). ||135||
They look at one another, and wear religious robes, but they are deluded and lost. ||135||
Seeing one another, they wear religious robes, go astray and wander at large.
seeing one another, put on (svaang) garbs and, astray, go wandering about. ||135||
79FV: O Kabir! (Following the pandits,) this whole world supposes a stone (idol) to be Parmesar and is worshipping it.
Kabeer, someone sets up a stone idol and all the world worships it as the Lord.
Kabir, setting up stone as god, all the mortal worship it.
Sri Kabir ji says: a (paahan) stone has been made Parmeshvar, and all — that is, much of — the world worships it.
MHFE: Is bharvaase = in this belief (that it is Parmatma). Boodde = drowned. Kaalee dhaar = in deep water (Note: the deeper the sea's water, the blacker its colour looks). ||136||
The people who believe that by worshipping a stone they are doing devotion to Parmatma — know them to be drowned in deep waters (from which no trace of them will ever be found). ||136||
Those who hold to this belief will be drowned in the river of darkness. ||136||
They, who abide in this belief, are drowned in the sable stream.
Those who rely on this alone are drowned in the stream of death. ||136||
4FAK: Obree = prison cell. Kaagad = (that is, the pandits') religious Shastras. Mas = ink. Mas ke = written in ink. Karam = (the code of) ritual. Kapaat = doors, strong doors.
O Kabir! (These pandits') Shastras are, as it were, a prison; the code of ritual written in ink (in these Shastras) is, as it were, the shut doors of that prison.
Kabeer, the paper is the prison, and the ink of rituals are the bars on the windows.
Kabir, the religious books form the prison and the ink of rituals its shutters.
Sri Kabir ji says: the religious Shastras are a (obree) cell of paper; the passages on ritual written in them with (mas) ink are its panels.
JY2R: Boree = drowned. Pirthamee = the earth, the people of the earth. Paarree baat = robbed on the road, carried out a robbery. Baat = road. ||137||

The stone idols (kept in this prison) have drowned the people of the earth (in the world-ocean); the pandits are committing robbery (that is, setting simple-hearted people to the ritual code of the Shastras and idol-worship, they rob them through offerings, alms and the like). ||137||
The stone idols have drowned the world, and the Pandits, the religious scholars, have plundered it on the way. ||137||
The stone-gods have drowned the world and the Pandits have plundered it on the way.

Setting the earth to the worship of stones, they have (boree) drowned it; in this way the pandits have robbed the road. Meaning, turning people from devotion, they have set them to deeds done for reward. So the thing of spiritual knowledge that was in the Shastras did not reach beings. ||137||
6150: Kal = tomorrow, the day that is to come tomorrow. Abahi = right now. Sui taal = that very moment.

(Continuing the thought of salok 132 he says:) O Kabir! (Never be lazy in remembering Parmatma.) What you plan to do tomorrow (that you will remember Him), do it right now (instead of starting remembrance tomorrow, start it right now; otherwise, saying "tomorrow, tomorrow" —)
Kabeer, that which you have to do tomorrow - do it today instead; and that which you have to do now - do it immediately!
Kabir, do now, what have you to do tomorrow and do that forthwith, what you have to do now.
Sri Kabir ji says: the dharma you are to do tomorrow, do (abahi) today. O brother, what you are to do today, do (sui taal) at once.
QUCA: Jau = when. Kaal = death. Paachhai = when the chance for devotion has passed, after the proper time. ||138||
when death comes overhead, at that time, the time having passed, nothing can be done. ||138||
Later on, you will not be able to do anything, when death hangs over your head. ||138||
Nothing would be done hereinafter, when the death hangs over your head.
For when death comes upon your head — meaning, when dying comes and seizes you — then afterwards nothing will be done. ||138||
CXXW: Aisa jant = such a person, who 'did not remember Ram'. Dhoee laakh = washed lac (which shines brightly).
O Kabir! I saw a person (who had never remembered Parmatma); he was (to look at from outside) like washed, shining lac.
Kabeer, I have seen a person, who is as shiny as washed wax.
Kabir, I have seen such a man, who is like the washed wax.
Seeing some hypocrite, Sri Kabir ji says: we have seen a hypocritical being like washed lac, which looks glossy from outside.
N6D5: Chanchal = clever, sharp. Bahu guna = very much. Mat heena = empty of sense. Naapaak = naa-paak, impure, of filthy life. ||139||
The person who has strayed from Prabhu's remembrance may look very clever and sharp, but in truth is empty of sense, because, separated from Prabhu, their life is filthy. ||139||
He seems very clever and very virtuous, but in reality, he is without understanding, and corrupt. ||139||
He appears to be clever and very virtuous, however, he is without understanding and unchaste.
In the same way he is fickle in speech — that is, a speaker of untruth — and (bahu guna) appears many-virtued to the eye only, and within is without good sense, impure — meaning, sinful. ||139||
9R6M: Budh = intellect. Kau = to. Tiskaar = tiraskaar, dishonour, insult.

O Kabir! (A person who has forgotten Prabhu's remembrance, though very clever, is senseless and deserves reproach, because their life stays low. But Prabhu's mercy has fallen on me; let alone the people of the world,) even Yamraj cannot reproach my intellect,
Kabeer, the Messenger of Death shall not compromise my understanding.
Kabir, death's myrmidon shall disgrace not my understanding.
Sri Kabir ji says: seeing my intellect, even Yama will not (tiskaar) dishonour me.
XS44: Jin = the (Sustainer) who, the sustaining Prabhu who. Jamooa = the poor wretch Yama, poor Yama (Note: the 'Yama' before whom the world trembles seems to the one who does devotion just an ordinary being created by Parmatma; they are not the least afraid of him). Su = Him (Parmatma). ||140||
because I have remembered that sustaining Prabhu who created this poor Yama. ||140||
I have meditated on the Lord, the Cherisher, who created this Messenger of Death. ||140||
I have meditated on that Lord, the Cherisher who has created this myrmidon of death.
I have chanted the Name of the Sustainer who (sirjia) created even this Yama who is killing people. ||140||
TN66: Kabir = the greatest of all, Parmatma, the supreme self. Bhaia = becomes, seems. Daas = servants (who worship Parmatma).

(To those who worship,) Parmatma (seems like) musk; all the devotees become His bumblebees (just as bumblebees are intoxicated by a flower's fragrance and do not go towards any foul-smelling place, so the devotees stay absorbed in the fragrance of Parmatma's love and do not turn towards the things of Maya).
Kabeer, the Lord is like musk; all His slaves are like bumble bees.
Kabir, God has become like musk and all his slaves have become bumble-bees.
Sri Kabir ji says: Parmeshvar, (kabir) greatest of all, has become fragrant like musk; so, to take that fragrance, all His servants have become like bumblebees.

F74P: Kabir kee bhagat = devotion to Parmatma. ||141||
The more they worship Parmatma, the more Parmatma comes to dwell in their hearts (who can reproach the intellect of such people?). ||141||
The more Kabeer worships Him, the more the Lord abides within his mind. ||141||
The more Kabir contemplates his Lord, the more, the Lord abides within his mind.
The more those servants worship that (kabir) great Hari, the more they come to dwell in that all-pervading Ram. ||141||
J3F9: Gahgach = in the press, in the bustle, in the throng. Kuttanb kai gahgach = in the turmoil of the family. Pario = lay, stayed caught. Kaanthai = on the bank, to one side, aside.
O Kabir! The person who stays caught in the press of the family — (the remembrance of) Parmatma stays aside (from their heart).
Kabeer, the mortal has fallen into the grip of family life, and the Lord has been set aside.
Kabir, man has fallen into the grip of family and the Lord has been set aside.
Sri Kabir ji says: this being lies (gahgach) wholly absorbed in the family, and so it has been left on the bank away from Ram; or, Ram has been left on the bank — meaning, was not attained.
23VX: Dharamraai ke = the messengers sent by Dharamraj. Aai pare = arrived. Beechahi = in the very midst. Dhoomdhaam = commotion. ||142||
While they are caught in the midst of this commotion, the messengers sent by Dharamraj arrive ('they did not remember Ram, and old age has come'). ||142||
The messengers of the Righteous Judge of Dharma descend upon the mortal, in the midst of all his pomp and ceremony. ||142||
The myrmidons of the Righteous Judge, descend on the mortal in the midst of his pomp.
Meanwhile Dharamrai's messengers have arrived. As soon as they came they raised a (dhooma) commotion in this (dhaam) house of the body — that is, made an uproar. ||142||
WTKL: Saakat te = than a person cut off from God. Sookar = pig. Bhala = good. Aachha = clean. Gaau = village.
O Kabir! (Than the saakat who, caught in the press of the family, forgets Parmatma) know even a pig to be better; (by eating the filth around the village) it keeps the village clean.
Kabeer, even a pig is better than the faithless cynic; at least the pig keeps the village clean.
Kabir, better than an infidel is a swine, which keeps the village clean.
Sri Kabir ji says: the pig is better than the saakat, for by eating filth it cleans the village and keeps it good.
CM8C: Bapura = poor, unfortunate. Koe naau na lai hai = no one even takes their name, no one even remembers them. ||143||
When that unfortunate saakat dies, no one even remembers them (however great they made themselves while alive). ||143||
When the wretched, faithless cynic dies, no one even mentions his name. ||143||
When he, the wretched materialist dies, no one even mentions his name.
For when that poor saakat dies, no one even takes their name, while people remember a dead pig; meaning, the saakat is lower even than a pig. ||143||
SDZQ: O Kabir! (What gain is there in gathering Maya alone, cut off from Prabhu?) The person who has gathered hundreds of thousands, tens of millions of rupees, adding them together with great pleading,
Kabeer, the mortal gathers wealth, shell by shell, accumulating thousands and millions.
Kabir, gathering shell by shell, man amasses lacs and millions.
Sri Kabir ji says: this being, adding cowrie to cowrie — that is, saving up — has gathered hundreds of thousands and tens of millions of rupees; meaning, gathered a great deal of Maya.
7DZS: Chaltee baar = at the time of leaving the world, at the time of death. Langottee = (Note: when a person dies, their relatives in ordinary circumstances bathe the body, dress it and cremate or bury it; it does not happen that they take off even the loincloth. But in old times merchants, on leaving home, would tie their rupees in a money-belt around the waist so they could not be stolen. The money-belt is a long, narrow pouch in which barely one rupee fits across; it is filled lengthwise with rupees, has ties at both ends, and with both ends closed is tied around the waist. A person who worried a great deal about their earnings would go about wearing it at all times. It seems that here by 'langottee' Kabir ji means the money-belt.) ||144||

(and cares so much for this gathered wealth that they go about with it tied at the waist in a money-belt) — even they gain nothing at the time of death; (their relatives) break off even their money-belt. ||144||
But when the time of his departure comes, he takes nothing at all with him. He is even stripped of his loin-cloth. ||144||
But at the time of departure, he gets nothing. Even his lion-piece is torn away from him.

But when setting out for the next world, nothing at all was gained. At the end the relatives broke off even the loincloth at the waist; meaning, the gold or silver waist-chain that the rich wear, they break that off too. ||144||
BWU0: Baisno = a devotee of Vishnu made by putting on tilak, rosary, discus-marks and the like. Maala melee chaar = put on four rosaries.

O Kabir! (Those who give up Prabhu's remembrance and earn wealth alone waste their life, for the wealth stays right here. But those who take outer garb alone to be the path of devotion earn nothing either.) If a person, putting on tilak and discus-marks and four rosaries, calls himself a Vaishnav devotee, he too has earned nothing.
Kabeer, what good is it to become a devotee of Vishnu, and wear four malas?
Kabir, what does it avail a man to become the follower of Vishnu and wear four rosaries?

For the sake of some hypocritical Vaishnav, Sri Kabir ji says: if one has become a Vaishnav through hypocrisy, what of it? And for show one has (melee) put on (chaar) four fine rosaries of sandalwood, tulsi and camphor around the neck.
CS9Q: Kanchan = gold. Baarha = of twelve grades, pure. Bheetar = within, in the mind. Bhangaar = lac, base metal. ||145||
(Because of this religious garb) he may look like pure gold from outside, but within him is nothing but dross. ||145||
On the outside, he may look like pure gold, but on the inside, he is stuffed with dust. ||145||
Externally he is gold twelve times purified, however, from within, he is stuffed with dust.

my heart was threaded onto the Guru's feet, and my ego mixed into the dust. ||157||

Z2ZW: Paal = (Sanskrit paali = skirt, boundary) bank, shore. Samuha = su-muh, up to the mouth, brim-full. Paal samuha = brim-full to the banks. Sarvar = pool.
O Kabir! The pool is brim-full (of water) to its banks, (but because of 'the burning of claims' no one sees this water, so) no one can drink this water.
Kabeer, the pool is filled to overflowing, but no one can drink the water from it.
Kabir, the entire tank is filled to the brim, however, no one can drink water therefrom.

Sri Kabir ji says: the pools that are the saints, who keep the (paal) embankments — that is, the code — are brim-full of the water of the Name. Meaning, even the liberated-while-living chant the Name. Without good fortune no ignorant being can drink this water of the Name.
7XDR: Tai paaio = you have found (the water). Bhar bhar = filling cups again and again, to your fill. ||170||
O Kabir! (You have escaped this 'burning') by good fortune you have seen this water; now drink it cup after cup (chant the Name joyfully with every breath). ||170||
By great good fortune, you have found it; drink it in handfuls, O Kabeer. ||170||
By great good fortune you have found it. Drink you it in handfuls, O Kabir.

So, O mind, the water of the Name you have found by great good fortune from the true company — now, Kabir ji says, fill it again and again with the cups of your ears — that is, by hearing — and drink it, that is, hold it. ||170||
7698: Parbhaate = at dawn (when the sun is about to rise, through the sun's splendour). Khisahi = grow dim, (the stars') light fades. Tiu = in the same way, through 'the burning of claims', under the influence of the inner heat born of possessions. Khisai = wastes away. Khisai sareer = this body wastes away; the spiritual light in this body grows weak; the senses' urge towards Prabhu fades. E dui akhar na khisahi = the two letters of the Name 'Ram' do not grow dim; the heat of possessions can have no effect on Parmatma's Name (Note: here "the two letters" means the two-lettered Name of Ram, Prabhu's Name).

O Kabir! (Just as, through the sun's splendour,) at dawn the stars (which shine in the settled quiet of night) grow dim, so, through the inner heat born of possessions, the light turned towards Prabhu fades from the senses.
Kabeer, just as the stars disappear at dawn, so shall this body disappear.
Kabir, as the stars disappear in morn, so does this body disappear.
Sri Kabir ji says: just as at dawn the stars (khisahi) disappear, so this body will disappear.
KBGF: Only Prabhu's Name stays beyond the effect of the heat of possessions. Kabir (instead of taking over the world's properties) keeps hold of that Name. ||171||
Only the letters of God's Name do not disappear; Kabeer holds these tight. ||171||
But these two letters of God disappear not, To them, Kabir is holding fast.
These two letters of Ram's Name, rara and mamma, do not (khisahi) go away. The one who keeps hold of them is the greatest of all; or, we are keeping hold of them. ||171||
D80N: Kothee = ("this world is the room of the True One") the world. Dis = from the side. Dah dis = from all ten sides, from every side. Aag laagee = 'the burning of claims' has caught; heat is arising in the mind from making possessions.
O Kabir! This world is, as it were, a house of wood that has caught (the fire of taking possessions) from every side;
Kabeer, the wooden house is burning on all sides.
Kabir, the house, of wood is on fire on ten sides.
Sri Kabir ji says: this house of wood that is the body has caught the fire of death from all ten directions.
VV44: Moorakh = the people who stayed careless of making possessions. Bhaag = running, fleeing, moving away from this 'burning of claims'. ||172||
the (people who think themselves) wise (and stay sitting in this fire) burn to death; the (ones these wise call) fools escape (burning) by running far away from this fire. ||172||
The Pandits, the religious scholars, have been burnt to death, while the illiterate ones run to safety. ||172||
The learned Brahmans have been burnt to death, while the illiterate persons have fled to safety.

The pandits, clever with the learning of the Shastras, proud of the body, have burnt to death in craving and the rest. The fools, without the learning of the Shastras, being free of pride, have run from the world and (ubre) been saved. ||172||
WQ46: Sansa = worry, 'burning'. Kaagad = paper (that is,) the accounts of worldly worry, the accounts of 'the burning of claims'. Bihaai dehi = wash away, set flowing such a current of joining the mind to Hari's feet that the accounts of 'the burning of claims' are swept away in that current of the Name.
O Kabir! (Through the blessing of this remembrance of Prabhu) remove the worries and burning of the world; wash away all the accounts of worry in the current of devotion.
Kabeer, give up your skepticism; let your papers float away.
Kabir! Cast off you your doubt and let go your paper knowledge, wash off in flood.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, remove doubt and wash away all the papers — that is, the Shastras too — that is, give them up.
VGAU: Baavan akhar = fifty-two letters (Sanskrit and Hindi have fifty-two letters. The Hindus sought to gain learning through Sanskrit or Hindi; so 'fifty-two letters' means 'learning'), learning. Sodh kai = refining (oneself), becoming reflective. ||173||

Becoming reflective through learning, join your mind to Prabhu's feet (that is, if you have had the chance to gain learning, then through it, instead of fretting over worldly possessions, become reflective and remember Parmatma). ||173||
Find the essence of the letters of the alphabet, and focus your consciousness on the Lord. ||173||
Imbibing the essence of the fifty-two letters, fix you your mind on the God's feet.
For all the Shastras and Vedas are in the fifty-two letters; so, (sodh) reflecting on their conclusion, fix the mind on Hari's feet. ||173||
8BSW: Santaee = the saint's nature, peace of mind. Jau = even if. Kottik = tens of millions. Asant = people full of vices, whose minds are not at peace.
O Kabir! (It is the very blessing of fixing the mind on Hari's feet that) the saint does not give up his peaceful nature, even if he has to deal with tens of millions of bad people.
Kabeer, the Saint does not forsake his Saintly nature, even though he meets with millions of evil-doers.
Kabir, the saint abandons not his saintliness, even though, he meets with millions of impious persons.
Sri Kabir ji says: even if millions upon millions of the unsaintly come to meet them — meaning, even if saakats meet them — still the saints do not give up their saintliness.
PCRK: Maliaagar = the sandalwood plant that grows on the Malaya mountain. Bhuyangam = snakes. Bedhio = surrounded. ||174||
The sandalwood plant stays surrounded by snakes, but it does not give up its inner coolness. ||174||
Even when sandalwood is surrounded by snakes, it does not give up its cooling fragrance. ||174||
Even when sandal is entwined with serpents, it leaves not its coolness.

Just as the (maliaagar) sandalwood, even when surrounded by many (bhuyangam) snakes, does not give up its coolness, so the saints do not give up their peaceful nature through the company of saakats, and, like sandalwood, make others cool too. ||174||
JPGP: O Kabir! When a person comes to know Parmatma (through remembrance), then (even while doing the work of the world) their mind stays cool and calm.
Kabeer, my mind is cooled and soothed; I have become God-conscious.
Kabir obtaining the Lord's knowledge, my mind has become refreshed.
Sri Kabir ji says: when we gained the knowledge of Braham, then our mind became cool.
J96X: Jin juaala = the fire of Maya that. Jaaria = has burnt. Su = that fire. Jan ke = for the servant, for the one who worships. Udak = water. Giaan = understanding, acquaintance. Braham = Parmatma. ||175||
The fire (of owning Maya) that has burnt the whole world stays (cool as) water for the person who worships. ||175||
The fire which has burnt the world is like water to the Lord's humble servant. ||175||
The fire that has burnt the world, that fire is like water to the Lord's slave.
The fire of Maya that has burnt the world has become like (udak) water for me, the servant, or for the saints; meaning, it cannot enchant them. ||175||
GCLF: Saaree = created, made. Sirjanhaar = Parmatma, maker of creation. Jaanai naahee koe = not everyone knows.
O Kabir! Not everyone knows that this (fire of Maya, which is burning the whole world) Parmatma Himself has made.
Kabeer, no one knows the Play of the Creator Lord.
Kabir, the world is the Creator Lord's play, but no one understands it.
Sri Kabir ji says: this creation, like a show, (saaree) made by the Creator Vahiguru — no one else knows it.
633W: Kai = or. Dhanee aapan = the Master Prabhu Himself. Deevaanee = one who stays in His court, who stays in His presence. ||176||

This secret is known by Prabhu Himself, or by the devotee who stays always joined to His feet (so the one who stays in His presence knows that the right way to escape the burning of Maya is to stay joined to the feet of the One who made Maya). ||176||
Only the Lord Himself and the slaves at His Court understand it. ||176||
Either the Master Himself, or one who is the slave of His court, understand it.

Either its (dhanee) Master Parmeshvar Himself knows it, or the servant whose intellect has become (deevaanee) intoxicated in the colour of His Name — that saint knows this show of the world to be unreal. ||176||
0FJ0: Bhalee bhaee = (the state of the person's mind) becomes good. Jo = when. Bhau = (Parmatma's) fear, the fear that forgetting Parmatma and wandering after Maya one must take many knocks. Disa = (other) directions, the wandering in other directions.

O Kabir! When (this) fear arises in a person (that forgetting Parmatma and wandering after Maya one must take many knocks), then the state of (their) mind becomes good; they forget all (other) directions (besides the shelter of Parmatma).
Kabeer, it is good that I feel the Fear of God; I have forgotten everything else.
Kabir, it is good, that I feel my Lord's fear and have forgotten everything else.
Sri Kabir ji says: it is good that the fear of that Master has fallen into the heart; through it all the directions of the world have been forgotten.

RXX4: Ora = hailstone. Gar = melting (with heat). Dhal = rolling down, flowing to a lower place. Kool = stream. ||177||
(The fear of Parmatma acts, as it were, as heat on a person's hardened mind; just as with heat) a hailstone melts back into water and, flowing down, joins the stream. ||177||
The hail-stone has melted into water, and flowed into the ocean. ||177||
Kabir, from hail, I have melted into water and flowing on, I have merged with my Lord, the ocean.

Just as the (ora) hailstone, melting, became water and then flowed down and joined the stream, so the person full of awe, giving up the sense of separate self, becoming pure consciousness, has merged into the stream that is Braham. ||177||
4HUG: Dhoor = dust, earth. Sakel kai = gathering. Pureea = town. Deh = body.
O Kabir! (Just as) gathering earth a town is built, so (gathering the five elements Parmatma) has made this body.
Kabeer, the body is a pile of dust, collected and packed together.
Kabir, collecting dust, the Lord has made the body like a physician's powder.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, gathering the (dhoor) earth — that is, the five elements, earth and the rest — (aa) especially, He has tied up a packet that is the body.
MFP8: Ko = of. Pekhna = beautiful to look at. Ant = in the end. Kheh kee kheh = born of dust, it mixed again into dust. ||178||
It looks beautiful for four days, but in the end it mixes back into the very dust it was made from. ||178||
It is a show which lasts for only a few days, and then dust returns to dust. ||178||
It is but four days play, ultimately, dust shall return to dust.
It is a (pekhna) puppet — that is, a play — of four days only. O brother, this body made of dust will become dust; meaning, it is bound to perish. ||178||
M8QJ: Sooraj chaand kai udai = for the shining of the sun and moon.

O Kabir! This body has been made (from the five elements) so that the sun and moon may rise in it (that is, that gentleness and coolness may arise; but these virtues can arise only if one meets the Guru and, through the Guru, joins Gobind's feet).
Kabeer, bodies are like the rising and setting of the sun and the moon.
Kabir, all the bodies are like the rising and setting of the sun and the moon.
Sri Kabir ji says: in the rising and setting of the sun and moon — that is, in day and night — all bodies have come into being.
CPHG: Without meeting the Guru-Parmatma, this body turns back into dust (that is, this human body goes utterly to waste). ||179||
Without meeting the Guru, the Lord of the Universe, they are all reduced to dust again. ||179||
However, without meeting with the Guru God, they all turn into dust again.
Without meeting through the Guru — meaning, without worship — this whole body turns back into dust; meaning, it has become fruitless. ||179||
5SAR: Jah = where, in which heart. Anbhau = inner understanding, knowledge, understanding of the right path of life. Bhai = worldly fears and worries. Bhau = dread, doubt.

In the heart in which understanding of the right path of life arises, no dangers (of burning, doubt, hardness and the like) remain. But in the heart in which (some) fear (of irritation, dread, cruelty and the like, which make one forget the peaceful life) is still present, Parmatma has not come to dwell.
Where the Fearless Lord is, there is no fear; where there is fear, the Lord is not there.
Where there is the fear-free Lord, no fear is there; where there is fear, the God comes not there.

The one in whose heart is the knowledge of the form that is direct experience has no fears of birth, death and the rest; and the ignorant one in whose heart Hari has not been attained, (tah) for them fear remains.
QS5H: Sunahu man maahi = listen with the mind, listen with attention. ||180||
I, Kabir, say this having reflected on it. O saints! Listen with attention. ||180||
Kabeer speaks after careful consideration; hear this, O Saints, in your minds. ||180||
Deliberating over this in his mind, Kabir says thus. Hear! O saints.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, hear these words which the saints have spoken after reflecting in their minds. ||180||
EY6S: Tin bihaai = their life passes. Sukh need = (even while lying in doubts and dreads) the sleep of heedlessness, in carelessness.
O Kabir! The people who have not understood (this secret of life) at all pass their life carelessly (even while wailing in this burning, doubt, hardness and the like);
Kabeer, those who do not know anything, pass their lives in peaceful sleep.
Kabir! They who know not; they pass their time in the sleep of peace.
Sri Kabir ji says: those who have known the world to be nothing — meaning, have known it to be unreal — their sleep of ignorance has (bihaai) gone, and they have attained the form of bliss.
CXEV: Boojha = understood. Boojhna = the thing worth understanding, that 'where there is direct experience there is no fear; where there is fear, Hari is not'. Pooree paree balaai = the whole burden has fallen on my neck; the hard task of facing the world's doubts is never forgotten. (Note: the sense here is not that Kabir ji dislikes walking this path. Kabir ji says that people, even while taking the blows of lust and the rest and crying 'alas, alas', are careless; but I am facing them day and night; and indeed this work is very hard.) ||181||
But (by the grace of 'the Guru-Gobind') I have understood that 'where there is direct experience there is no fear; where there is fear, Hari is not'; this never leaves my mind at any time. ||181||
But I have understood the riddle; I am faced with all sorts of troubles. ||181||
I, who have understood the riddle, am face to face with a whole host of troubles.
(Hamhu) For us who took the world to be real, that very understanding has fallen as a whole burden around our neck. ||181||
UMEX: Maare = the one who is struck (by burning, doubt and the like). Bahut pukaaria = cries out a great deal, suffers greatly. Peer = blow, pain. Peer pukaarai aur = the more the pain (of burning, doubt and the like) rises, the more they cry out, the more they suffer.
O Kabir! The person who is struck (by burning, doubt and the like) cries out a great deal; the more that pain rises, the more they suffer (and yet they do not let go of Maya).
Kabeer, those who are beaten cry a lot; but the cries of the pain of separation are different.
Kabir! The evil persons weep much, however, different is the weeping of the saints.

Those who are without detachment are the (kabir) greatest (maare) wretches. They cry out a great deal — meaning, without practice they only talk. And the (peer) great, worshipful great-souled saints cry out in another way — meaning, their words go with practice.
JDDQ: Chot = the blow of the Word. Maranm kee = piercing the heart. Rahio thaur = I have stayed in my place; I am no longer one to cry out; neither do burning, doubt and the like strike me, nor do I cry out. ||182||

I, Kabir, have been struck by the blow of the Guru's Word, which has pierced my heart; now I have settled in my place (that is, at Prabhu's feet). (This burning, doubt and the like cannot trouble me at all.) ||182||
Struck by the Mystery of God, Kabeer remains silent. ||182||
Smitten with the stroke of God, love on the mysterious organ, Kabir fell at the spot.
Sri Kabir ji says: those who, through those saints, have been struck by the blow of love for the Husband are settled in the (thaur) infinite — that is, in Vahiguru, the limit of all. ||182||
4VKD: Sel = spear, the spear of the Guru's Word. Suhelee = giving comfort (Note: the blow of burning, doubt and the like gives pain, but the blow of the spear of the Guru's Word brings comfort). Lei usaas = draws deep sighs, a longing arises to meet Prabhu.
O Kabir! The blow of the spear of the Guru's Word is truly comforting. In the person struck by this blow (like a bride in separation) a longing arises to meet the Husband-Prabhu.
Kabeer, the stroke of a lance is easy to bear; it takes away the breath.
Kabir! Illustrious is the stroke of a lance, it draws out the breath as soon as it strikes.
Sri Kabir ji says: the blow of the (sel) spear that takes the breath as soon as it strikes is (suhelee) easy to bear;
QUG9: The (fortunate) person who keeps taking the blow of the Guru's Word — I am (ever ready to be) the servant of that worshipful person. ||183||
But one who endures the stroke of the Word of the Shabad is the Guru, and I am his slave. ||183||
He who endures the stroke of the Guru's word, he is the Guru and I his slave.

but the person who bears the blow of the Guru's Word, or of harsh words, is like a Guru to me, and I am their servant. ||183|| ☬ Some mullah was giving the call to prayer from a high place; for his sake Sri Kabir ji says:
VK8C: Mulaan = O mullah! Kia chadhahi = there is no gain in climbing. Munaare kia chadhahi = climbing the minaret does you yourself no good, giving the call does you yourself no good. Bahra = deaf (Note: a deaf person can be deceived by speaking loudly of respect and love while cursing softly; but God understands even the state of the heart; He cannot be deceived).
O Kabir! O mullah! Climbing the minaret of the mosque is doing you yourself no good. God is not deaf (He knows the state of your heart too; He cannot be deceived).
Kabeer: O Mullah, why do you climb to the top of the minaret? The Lord is not hard of hearing.
Kabir, why does Mulla go up a minaret (to make loud sound)? The Lord is not deaf.
O mullah, why are you climbing the minaret and giving the call? The Lord of all has not become (bahra) deaf.
QE77: Ja kaaran = for whose prayer. Joe = see, search. ||184||
The One (for whose prayer) you are giving the call — see Him within your own heart (He dwells within you. There is no peace within you; you are only calling people). ||184||
Look within your own heart for the One, for whose sake you shout your prayers. ||184||
For whose sake, you make a loud prayer-call, He is in your heart.
For the One to whom you give the call, (joe) see Him within your own heart. ||184||
LW7H: O Sheikh! If there is no contentment within you, there is no gain in going on hajj to the Kaaba;
Why does the Shaykh bother to go on pilgrimage to Mecca, if he is not content with himself?
Why should the Shaikh, who is without contentment, go for a pilgrimage to Mecca?
O Sheikh! Without (sabooree) contentment, if one goes to the Kaaba and does hajj, what of it? Meaning, it is fruitless.
2STX: Dil saabat = wholeness of heart, peace of heart, steadiness. Ta kau = to them. Kaha khudaai = God is nowhere. ||185||
because, O Kabir, for the person whose own heart has not found peace, God is nowhere. ||185||
Kabeer, one whose heart is not healthy and whole - how can he attain his Lord? ||185||
He, whose mind is not whole, how can he attain to his God?
Sri Kabir ji says: the one whose (dil) heart has no (saabat) cleanness — where does God meet them? Meaning, He does not. ||185||
SA62: O Kabir! Worship God; only by worship does the vice of the heart go,
Kabeer, worship the Lord Allah; meditating in remembrance on Him, troubles and pains depart.
Kabir, perform you the meditation of your God, contemplating whom, the troubles depart.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, worship Allah, by remembering whom your pain of birth and death will go away.
QMLZ: Balantee = the burning fire, the burning fire of craving. Naanh = through the Name. ||186||
God is revealed in the heart, and through the blessing of this worship the burning fire of greed in the heart is put out. ||186||
The Lord shall be revealed within your own heart, and the burning fire within shall be extinguished by His Name. ||186||
The Lord shall become manifest within your mind and your burning fire shall be quenched.
And when the Lord of all is revealed in the heart, the fire of craving that was burning will be put out by chanting His (naai) Name. ||186||
JPF6: Joree keeai = by using force. Halaal = lawful, fit to offer, fit to be sacrificed in God's name.

O Kabir! (Tell the mullah that) using force on anyone is cruelty; (you catch an animal, say "Bismillah" and slaughter it, and) you say that this (slaughtered animal) has become fit to be sacrificed in God's name (and that by this sacrifice God is pleased with you); (but you eat the meat yourself. Sins are not forgiven like this; think sometime —)
Kabeer, to use force is tyranny, even if you call it legal.
Kabir, to use force is tyranny, even if it be lawful.
Sri Kabir ji says: killing a goat and the like by force is cruelty, and having killed it they call it 'made halaal'.
751V: when the account of your deeds is taken in God's court, what will your state be? ||187||
When your account is called for in the Court of the Lord, what will your condition be then? ||187||
When your account is called in the Lord's court then what shall be your condition?
When in Dharamrai's office your account is asked of you, what will your state be then? That is, only a bad state. ||187||
4ZVW: Khoob khaana = good food. Lon = salt.
O Kabir! (Tell the mullah plainly that rather than eating meat on the pretext of sacrifice) it is better to eat khichri with only tasty salt in it.
Kabeer, the dinner of beans and rice is excellent, if it is flavored with salt.
Kabir sublime is the dinner of rice of pulse boiled together, in which there is delicious salt.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, eating khichri is good — that is, fine — the khichri in which ghee like nectar and salt are put.
GEXM: Hera = meat. Kaarne = for the purpose of, with the intention. Kattaavai kaun = I am not ready to cut. ||188||
I am not ready, when the intention to eat meat and bread is my own, to go about slaughtering (some animal, crying out 'sacrifice'). ||188||
Who would cut his throat, to have meat with his bread? ||188||
Who will have his throat cut for meat with his bread?

For who would have himself cut afterwards for the sake of eating bread with meat, killing beings in the (hera) hunt? Meaning, by killing a being one must later have one's own head cut off by it. ||188||
HP55: Tab jaaneeai = then know, only then understand. Gur laaga = the Guru has taken hold, has been met. Tan taap = the troubles of the body, the pains and troubles that burn the body.

O Kabir! (Putting on the sacred thread, the Hindu thinks, "I have taken such-and-such Brahmin as my guru"; but) know that the Guru has been met only when attachment to Maya goes (from the heart of the one who takes the Guru), when the troubles that burn the body are wiped away.
Kabeer, one is known to have been touched by the Guru, only when his emotional attachment and physical illnesses are eradicated.
Kabir, then alone the Guru is deemed to have touched the heart, if man's worldly love and bodily ailments are effaced.
Sri Kabir ji says: the Guru's teaching is known to have taken hold of the disciple when all the fevers born of attachment are wiped from their subtle (tan) mind.
YMC0: Harakh = joy. Sog = worry. Daajhai nahee = does not burn. Aapahi aap = He alone is seen everywhere. ||189||
When neither joy nor grief burns the mind — reaching such a state, Parmatma Himself alone is seen everywhere. ||189||
He is not burned by pleasure or pain, and so he becomes the Lord Himself. ||189||
Weal and woe burn him not and then he becomes God himself.
When the fire of joy and grief does not (daajhai) burn them, then one's own self becomes one with Hari. ||189||
1HJB: Bhed = difference. Ek bichaar = a particular thing to understand.
O Kabir! (Giving the sacred thread, the Brahmin also teaches worship and recitation of Ram; but) there is a difference even in saying "Ram, Ram"; in it too there is one thing to understand.
Kabeer, it does make a difference, how you chant the Lord's Name, 'Raam'. This is something to consider.
Kabir! There is a secret in worshipping 'Ram'; Therein lies a point worthy of consideration.

Someone said: what is the Guru's teaching for, since everyone takes Ram's Name? For his sake Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, there is a difference in uttering Ram's Name. What difference? In it there is a difference of reflection alone.
7KDZ: Sabhai = all beings. Soee = that same Ram, that same Ram. Kautakhaar = players in religious pageants. ||190||

One Ram is the one every being remembers (this is the all-pervading Ram; remembering Him is the duty of every human being). But this same Name of Ram is taken by pageant-players too (putting on shows in their pageants) (this Ram is the incarnate Ram, the son of King Dasrath; this idol-worship is useless). ||190||
Everyone uses the same word for the son of Dasrath and the Wondrous Lord. ||190||
The same word, every one uses for Dasrath's son and the same word for the Wondrous Lord.

For all the saints utter that same Name of Ram and attain well-being, and the (kautak) showmen — that is, pageant-players and the like — utter that same Name of Ram. Meaning, they speak it for worldly success, and the saints, through reflection understanding Him as all-pervading, attain peace. ||190||
VRWE: Ramai Ram kahu = remember Ram's Name at every moment. Bibek = discernment, recognition. Kahibe maahi = in saying, in remembering.
O Kabir! Always chant Ram's Name, but while chanting keep this in mind —
Kabeer, use the word 'Raam', only to speak of the All-pervading Lord. You must make that distinction.
Kabir, Him alone call you 'Ram' who is Omnipresent. We should discriminate between the two while mentioning them.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, utter Ram's Name alone, but in uttering there is one (bibek) discernment.
14BL: Anekahi = in countless beings. Samaana ek = stayed in only one body. ||191||
that one Ram pervades countless beings (chanting His Name is every person's dharma), but one Ram (Dasrath's son) came in only one body (became an incarnation; chanting him can do no good). ||191||
One 'Raam' is pervading everywhere, while the other is contained only in himself. ||191||
One 'Ram', 'the God', is pervading among all, while the other Ram Chander is contained in himself alone.

For the one, the reflective saint, has through reflection merged into the One Ram — that is, become one. And the mind of the other, the showmen, has merged into countless things; because of this they do not attain liberation. Or: the one, through devotion with separateness, met Parmeshvar over countless births, and the other, doing devotion of oneness, merged into Ram in one birth. ||191||
WRKY: Ja ghar = in which houses. Saadh = good people, those who have tamed their minds, members of the true company. Na seveeahi = are not served. Seva = worship, devotion.

O Kabir! (Worship of idols, and service of the Brahmin on every festival day — this is the teaching the Brahmin god is giving his believers. The poor believers too, by worshipping idols and serving the Brahmin, think themselves proper and pure Hindus; but the real truth is that) the houses in which good people are not served and Parmatma is not worshipped —
Kabeer, those houses in which neither the Holy nor the Lord are served
Kabir, the houses, in which the saints are not served nor God is contemplated;
