That alone, which he chewed while it was being grounded avails the mortal.
What was chewed while grinding — that alone went with one; meaning, the worship done while the breaths lasted — that alone helped at the end. ||215||
7HF3: O Kabir! (The person who goes to a holy place every day and worships, and then spends the whole day earning by cheating and fraud, is not unaware that this is wrong; their) mind knows everything, yet knowing, they go on committing (the) sin (of earning by cheating).
Kabeer, the mortal knows everything, and knowing, he still makes mistakes.
Kabir, man knows everything and knowingly commits he sins.
Sri Kabir ji says: this mind knows all about sin and merit, but knowing, it still does wrong.
J5NE: Kuslaat = comfort, well-being. Haath deep = (if there is) a lamp in the hand. Kooe = into a well. ||216||

(Devotion to Parmatma is a burning lamp that is to show a person the way on the dark journey of life and save them from falling into the pit of vices; but) what comfort is that lamp if, with the lamp in our hand, we still fall into the well? ||216||
What good is a lamp in one's hand, if he falls into the well? ||216||
What use is it to have a lamp in his hand, if the man still falls into a well?

Just as when one takes a lamp in one's own hand and still goes and falls into a well, what well-being is there? In the same way, how can this being be well, who even after reading the Vedas and Shastras has stayed full of vices? ||216||
UH7B: Sujaan = wise, the knower of every heart. Laagee = attached. Ajaan = ignorant, senseless, foolish.

O Kabir! (If you want to keep your 'mind joined to Niranjan', remember that) this foolish world (that is, attachment to relatives and earning by cheating) puts obstacles in the way of the love formed with Parmatma, the knower of every heart;
Kabeer, I am in love with the All-knowing Lord; the ignorant ones try to hold me back.
Kabir, I am in love with my Omniscient Lord. The ignorant ones restrain me.
Sri Kabir ji says: seeing our love attached to (sujaan) Vahiguru, the ignorant beings forbid it.
QPS8: Ta siu = from that (wise Prabhu). Kiu banai = how can it look fitting? How can it seem beautiful? It does not look fitting, does not seem beautiful. Jeea = soul. Barjai = forbids, puts obstacles. ||217||
(and in falling for this deception there is only loss, because) this soul and life, given by Parmatma, cannot look beautiful (cannot be at ease in any state) separated from Him. ||217||
How could I ever break with the One, who owns our soul and breath of life. ||217||
How can I break with Him, with whom belong my soul and vital-breath?
But how can it do, broken off in love from the One who has given this soul and breath of life? ||217||
SAMD: Mandap = canopies, mansions. Het kar = with fondness, with eagerness. Savaar = decorating again and again. Kaahe marahu = why are you dying a spiritual death?

(A soul separated from Prabhu, the giver of the soul, cannot stay at ease: 'ta siu tootee kiu banai'; so) O Kabir! (forgetting that giver of the soul,) why are you dying a spiritual death, decorating houses and mansions again and again with such eagerness?
Kabeer, why kill yourself for your love of decorations of your home and mansion?
Kabir, why harm yourself with excessive love and decoration of yours home and temples?
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother! Why do you die decorating rooms to live in and (mandap) places of assembly, halls of audience and the like?
LFV5: Kaaraj = work, purpose, need. Ghanee = more. Ta = then. ||218||

Your own need is met by three and a half cubits of ground (for every day, when you sleep, you use only about this much, according to your height); and if (you are rather tall and) you need a little more ground, you might use three and three-quarter cubits. ||218||
In the end, only six feet, or a little more, shall be your lot. ||218||
Three and a halt or at the most three and three quarters cubes of land shall be of avail to you.
For your purpose only three and a half cubits of earth are needed; and if more is needed, for placing a pillow and so on, then three and three-quarter cubits are plenty. ||218||
E1NA: O Kabir! (Instead of keeping 'the mind joined to Niranjan', you keep thinking thoughts of Maya all day; but) nothing comes of my thinking; Parmatma does not do what I think (that is, what we keep thinking).
Kabeer, whatever I wish for does not happen. What can I accomplish by merely thinking?
Kabir, the Lord does not do according to my desire. What can be achieved by my desiring?
Sri Kabir ji says: what I think, Hari does not do; then what comes of my thinking?
FMT4: Prabhu does what He Himself thinks, and what Parmatma thinks does not even come into our minds. ||219||
The Lord does whatever He wishes; it is not up to me at all. ||219||
The God does what He Himself desires (as per His will) and not according to what is on my mind.
For Hari does only what He Himself has thought, which is not in my mind at all. ||219||
ZC8F: O Kabir! (What is in the power of beings?) Prabhu Himself creates worries and thoughts of the world in the minds of beings; Prabhu Himself also grants the state in which a person becomes free of these worries and thoughts.
God Himself makes the mortals anxious, and He Himself takes the anxiety away.
God Himself produced anxiety in man and Himself frees him from anxiety.
So Vahiguru Himself causes worry, and He Himself also gives freedom from worry.
3SAW: O Nanak! We should sing the praises of that very Prabhu who takes care of all beings (that is, pray to Prabhu alone and ask for the gift of staying free of the worries and thoughts of the world). ||220||
O Nanak, praise the One, who takes care of all. ||220||
Nanak, praise you Him, who takes care of all.
Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji utters: so, O brother, let us always praise that very Akal Purakh who, (saar) taking news of all beings, sustains them. ||220||
LQE6: O Kabir! The person who does not remember Parmatma (and the result of not remembering is just this: they keep thinking thoughts of the world) wanders about in the greed (of the world).
Kabeer, the mortal does not remember the Lord; he wanders around, engrossed in greed.
Kabir, man contemplates not his Lord and wanders about engrossed in greed.
Sri Guru ji says through Kabir ji: this being has not remembered Ram, and, caught in the greed of Maya, has kept wandering in worldly affairs.
V8YZ: Mar gaia = dies a spiritual death; the virtues vanish from one's life. Audh = lifespan. Punee = is completed, runs out. Khin maah = in the blink of an eye, suddenly; one is not yet sated with vices when suddenly ... ||221||

Committing sin after sin, that (unfortunate) person dies a spiritual death (the high spiritual life within them comes to an end), and they are not yet sated with vices when suddenly their life runs out. ||221||
Committing sins, he dies, and his life ends in an instant. ||221||
He dies committing sins and his life comes to and end in a moment.
When the lifespan was complete, still committing sins, one died in an instant. ||221||
SG1H: Kaarvee = a small pitcher, a small pot. Keval = purely. Dhaat = substance, origin.
O Kabir! (Know) this body as an unbaked pot; (take) its substance to be nothing but unbaked clay.
Kabeer, the body is like a clay vessel or a brittle metal pot.
Kabir, the body is an earthen vessel or only a frail metal.
Sri Kabir ji says: this unbaked body, being only (dhaat) of Maya, is an unbaked (kaarvee) new pot.
Y95G: Saabat = (see salok no. 185: 'ja kee dil saabat nahee'; 'saabat' means purity) pure, clean. Rakhahi = if you want to keep. Bhaj = remember. Binathee = spoiled, destroyed. Baat = matter. ||222||
If you want to keep it pure (from bad outside influences), remember Parmatma's Name; otherwise know this game (of human birth) as already spoiled (that is, it will surely be spoiled). ||222||
If you wish to keep it safe and sound, then vibrate and meditate on the Lord; otherwise, the thing shall break. ||222||
If you wish to keep it whole then remember you your Lord, otherwise this thing shall perish.
O brother! If you want to keep it whole — that is, make it fruitful — then remember Ram; otherwise this (baat) matter will perish in vain. ||222||
9ZFN: Keso = Keshav (keshaah prashastaah santi asya = the one with long hair), Parmatma. Asaar = being careless, heedless, staying careless about vices.
O Kabir! (If you want to 'keep' this body 'pure' from vices,) let us keep remembering Parmatma's Name at every moment, and never become careless about vices at any time.
Kabeer, chant the Name of the Beautifully-haired Lord; do not sleep unaware.
Kabir, recite you the Name of the Beautifully-haired Lord and sleep not heedlessly.
Sri Kabir ji says: crying "Keso, Keso", let us always (kookeeai) utter the Name; let us not sleep (asaar) unaware of it.
WDZN: If we keep remembering Parmatma day and night (at every moment), then at some time or other that Prabhu does hear the prayer of the being (and saves them from dying a spiritual death). ||223||
Chanting His Name night and day, the Lord will eventually hear your call. ||223||
Calling out the Name, night and day, the Lord shall sometime hear the cry.
For by calling out the Name day and night, that Hari will surely hear the call some time. ||223||
C4Q9: Kaia = body. Kajlee ban = the name of a forest near Rishikesh and Haridwar where elephants live; a dense forest (Note: when a person forgets the remembrance of Parmatma, all their senses turn towards vices, and countless vices such as lust rise up. Take such a body to be a forest in which countless vices are, as it were, dense trees). Bhaia = (if one does not cry 'Keso, Keso', this body) becomes (a forest full of the trees of vice). Kunchar = elephant. May mant = mad matt, intoxicated in its own rut.

O Kabir! (If we do not cry 'Keso, Keso', if we do not remember Parmatma, then, because countless vices arise,) this human body becomes, as it were, the 'Kajlee forest', in which the mind-elephant roams intoxicated in its own rut.
Kabeer, the body is a banana forest, and the mind is an intoxicated elephant.
Kabir, the body is garden of plantains and the mind is an elephant, intoxicated with the wine of worldliness.
Sri Kabir ji says: the body has become the Kajlee forest; in it the mind-elephant is intoxicated with the (may) wine of ego.
E9T6: Ankas = the iron hook with which an elephant is driven. Ratan = excellent like a jewel. Khevat = driver. ||224||
Only the Guru's excellent knowledge can become the hook to keep this elephant under control; only some fortunate Gurmukh is able to drive (the mind-elephant, using this hook of knowledge). ||224||
The jewel of spiritual wisdom is the prod, and the rare Saint is the rider. ||224||
The jewel of Divine knowledge is the goad and some rare saint is the elephant-driver.

To bring it under control there is the (ankas) hook of knowledge, set with the jewel of detachment; and the (khevat) driver, in the form of the mahout, is some rare saint. A khevat is the boatman who steers a boat, but here, in the sense of driving, the mahout is meant. ||224||
3UZF: Kotharee = pouch, purse. Paarakh = the assayer, the one who knows the worth.

O Kabir! Parmatma's Name is the most precious thing (in the world); (to keep this treasure safe) make your mouth a pouch, and open your mouth only before some Gurmukh who knows the worth of this jewel (that is, praise Prabhu's Name in the sangat).
Kabeer, the Lord's Name is the jewel, and the mouth is the purse; open this purse to the Appraiser.
Kabir, Lord is the emerald and mouth its purse. Open you the purse only before an assayer.
Sri Kabir ji says: the jewel of Ram's Name, which is in the (kotharee) pouch of the mouth — O brother, open it before the one who can assay it; meaning, give this teaching to a worthy seeker.
NUF0: Gaahakee = the buyer of the Name-jewel. Mahage mol = at a heavy price (Note: in this body-forest the mind roams free like an elephant in rut. Whether animal, bird or human, giving up one's freedom is the greatest sacrifice for anyone; to buy anything in exchange for this freedom of the mind is to pay the costliest of prices), by handing over the mind. ||225||
When some buyer who knows the worth of the Name-jewel arrives in the sangat, they hand their mind over to the Guru and buy the Name-jewel. ||225||
If a buyer can be found, it will go for a high price. ||225||
If any purchaser be found, he would take it, at a very high price.
For when some buyer in the form of a seeker comes and meets you, they will take this Name-jewel at a costly price; meaning, they will offer everything — body, mind, wealth and all. ||225||
0RHQ: Jaanio nahee = (the person who) did not know the worth. Paalio = kept rearing. Katak = army. Katak kutamb = a large family.
(But) O Kabir! The person who does not understand the worth of Parmatma's Name-jewel keeps (forgetting the Name-jewel and, all their life,) only rearing a large family;
Kabeer, the mortal does not know the Lord's Name, but he has raised a very large family.
Kabir, man knows not the Lord's Name, however, he has brought up a very big family.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother! You did not know Ram's Name — that is, you did not remember it — and you kept rearing a family like an army; meaning, all relatives are plunderers of the being.
5C3P: Mar gaio = died a spiritual death. Baahar = outside worldly affairs, (that is,) free of them. Bamb = sound, news. Baahar bhaee na bamb = coming out of worldly affairs, not even the sound of Ram's Name ever came from their mouth. ||226||

Wearing themselves out in the affairs of the world, that person dies a spiritual death; coming out of these struggles, the sound of Ram's Name never comes from their mouth (they never get free of these struggles, nor do they ever utter Parmatma's Name with their mouth). ||226||
He dies in the midst of his worldly affairs, and then he is not heard in the external world. ||226||
He dies in the midst of worldly affairs and is heard no more in the outer world.
So you died in the midst of worldly affairs, but the (bamb) word of uttering the Name never came out of your mouth; meaning, you did not utter the Name. ||226||
P20V: Kere = of. Maatuke = blinkings. Aakhee kere maatuke = the time of a blink of the eyes. Gaee bihaai = (life) passes.

O Kabir! (See the state of that unfortunate one who, not knowing the worth of Prabhu's Name, spends all their life rearing a family and never utters Prabhu's Name! Bit by bit, unnoticed,) their life passes, a blink of the eyes at a time, moment by moment;
Kabeer, in the blink of an eye, moment by moment, life is passing by.
O Kabir, the life passes away, in the blinking moment of an eye and moment by moment.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother! In the (maatuke) blinking — that is, the opening and closing — of the eyes, moment by moment, life has passed.
504W: Damaama = kettledrum. Aai deea = comes and beats. ||227||
Even so, their mind does not let go of the entanglement (of family); at last the messengers of death come and beat the drum of death. ||227||
The mortal does not give up his worldly entanglements; the Messenger of Death walks in and beats the drum. ||227||
Man leaves not his entanglements and death's courier walks in and beats his drum.
But even now the mind does not let go of entanglements; meanwhile Yama has come and beaten the (damaama) drum of death. ||227||
7MJX: Tarvar = tar-var, a beautiful tree. Tar = tree. Bairaag = detachment.
O Kabir! (In this world, burning in the heat of vices,) Prabhu's Name is a beautiful tree.
Kabeer, the Lord is the tree, and disillusionment with the world is the fruit.
Kabir, the Lord is as a tree and the Lord's love is like its fruit.
Sri Kabir ji says: detachment is a tree, and in it the fruit is the attainment of Ram.
KGM0: Chhaaia = shade. Jin = the one (the saadh, the Gurmukh) who. Baad bibaad = quarrels and wrangling, the entanglement of Maya. ||228||

The person who has ended the quarrels and wrangling (of these vices within them) is that Gurmukh who is, as it were, the shade of this tree. (The fortunate person who takes the support of this shade, to escape that heat, gains) the fruit of detachment. ||228||
The Holy man, who has abandoned useless arguments, is the shade of the tree. ||228||
The saint, who has abandoned vain strifes, is like its shade.
The saints who have abandoned the (baad) futile (bibaad) quarrels of the world — those excellent saints are the shade of this tree; meaning, they have become peace itself. ||228||
9DZW: Baarah maas = all twelve months, always. Phalant = gives fruit.
O Kabir! (Staying in the company of that 'saadh' who 'jin tajia baad bibaad', you too, in the soil of your heart,) sow such a seed (of Parmatma's Name) as always keeps giving fruit;
Kabeer, plant the seeds of such a plant, which shall bear fruit throughout the twelve months,
Kabir, sow you the seed of such a plant, which bears fruit throughout the twelve months of year,
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother! Sow such a seed of the Name as gives fruit in all twelve months.
ZCRA: Seetal = cool, cooling, peace-giving. Chhaaia = shade, support. Gahir = depth, steadiness, detachment. Pankhee = (that is, your) senses. Kel = delight. ||229||

When we take its support, coolness settles within; the fruit gained is that the mind becomes steady against the 'baad bibaad' of the world; and all the senses (which before wandered from place to place for food like birds, now) enjoy the delight (of Prabhu's Name). ||229||
with cooling shade and abundant fruit, upon which birds joyously play. ||229||
and whose shade is cool, fruits are abundant and on which the birds joyously play.
Its shade is peace, and the deep, profound Parmatma is its fruit; and the bird in the form of the seeker plays — that is, eating this fruit, meaning holding it within, finds happiness. ||229||
TBYP: Daata = the one who gives the gift of Prabhu's Name. Daya = love for all beings. Upkaaree jeevant = one who lives only in doing good to others, who spends all of life in doing good.

O Kabir! That 'saadhu' (who 'jin tajia baad bibaad') spends all of their life doing good; that 'saadhu', the giver of the gift of Prabhu's Name, is, as it were, a beautiful tree (for this whole world burning in vices); from them the gift of 'compassion for all beings' is received.
Kabeer, the Great Giver is the tree, which blesses all with the fruit of compassion.
Kabir, the Beneficent Lord is the Tree, whose fruit is compassion and who does good to all the beings.
Sri Kabir ji says: the True Guru, who is the giver, is like a tree, bearing the fruit of compassion, and to the very end does good to beings.
DAWV: Pankhee = the birds of this world-tree, all beings. Disaavaree = disha avar, to other and other directions, to other sides, into other and other affairs. Birkha = the tree that gives the 'Name' (the saadhu). Suphal phalant = keeps giving only the beautiful gift of 'compassion', keeps teaching everyone to love all beings. Suphal = su-phal, beautiful fruit. ||230||
Worldly beings stay busy in other and other affairs, but the Gurmukh 'saadh' always keeps teaching: treat everyone with compassion and love. ||230||
When the birds migrate to other lands, O Tree, you bear the fruits. ||230||
On migrating to another country, birds say 'O tree, may you bear sublime fruits'.

The birds in the form of seekers, taking from them the fruit of compassion, go off (disaavaree) in other directions blessing the tree in the form of the Guru, and say: "O tree! May you always stay laden with the fruits of excellent virtues." ||230||
4CPS: Saadhoo sang = the company of the saadhu (who 'jin tajia baad bibaad'). Lilaat = forehead. Likhia hoi lilaat = if it is written on the forehead, if one has good fortune.
O Kabir! The company of that saadhu, the Gurmukh who 'jin tajia baad bibaad', is gained by the person who has very good fortune.
Kabeer, the mortal finds the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, if he has such destiny written upon his forehead.
Kabir, if it be so writ on his brow, then man is blessed with the saints' society.
Sri Kabir ji says: the company of saints is gained when a good destiny is written on the (lilaat) forehead.

ALXG: Mukat = freedom from 'baad bibaad'. Thaak = obstruction. Avghat ghaat = a hard mountain path (Note: trying to stay safe from the 'baad bibaad' of the world is like climbing a high mountain). ||231||
The fruit gained from their company is this: one is freed from the 'baad bibaad' of the world, and no vice whatever obstructs the way on this hard journey. ||231||
He obtains the treasure of liberation, and the difficult road to the Lord is not blocked. ||231||
Thiswise the wealth of emancipation is attained and the difficult road to God is obstructed not.

Through the company of those saints the treasure of liberation is gained, and through the company of saints the (avghat) hard (ghaat) places in the next world — or the vices, lust and the rest — cannot obstruct. ||231||
V41B: Bannh = (under the letter 'n' there is a half 'h') having tied. Vannjaa = should I go. Ghat = having thrown. Potlee = a small bundle. ||2||
(I too) have tied up and lifted the little bundle (of the 'world'); where can I go and throw it down? (that is, letting go of attachment to the world is no easy task). ||2||
I am so accustomed to walking in the ways of the world. I have tied and picked up the bundle; where can I go to throw it away? ||2||
I have tied the bundle of the Lord's meditation and lifted over my head, now, how can I go anywhere without it?

Then he says: this bundle of fakir-hood, which I have tied up and lifted onto my head — that is, taken on — where should I (ghat) put it down — that is, throw it — and (vannjaa) go? But it cannot be thrown away, so I will stay just like this. ||2|| ☬ Having said this, Farid ji set aside his thought and went on. Behind him, all those melons turned into human heads. Then the owner of the field, knowing it as the fruit of dishonouring a saint, went from there and fell at Farid ji's feet, and told him of his household. Hearing of his sorrows, Sri Farid ji says, with reference to him:
V4K5: O Kabir! (Since freedom from the 'baad bibaad' of the world is gained only by keeping the company of the saadhu, therefore) one ghari, half a ghari, a quarter of a ghari —
Kabeer, whether is is for an hour, half an hour, or half of that,
Kabir, even for a ghari, half a ghari, or even half of that;
Sri Kabir ji says: one ghari, or half a ghari, or even half of a half —
D9H4: Goste = goshti, conversation, meeting (Note: the word goshti has two meanings: (1) discourse, debate, conversation; (2) meeting, company. As in 'Sidh Gosti' = (1) debate with the siddhas, (2) union with Parmatma. See my teeka on 'Sidh Gosti'). Keene = is done. ||232||
however long one keeps the company of Gurmukhs, from it there is (in spiritual life) nothing but gain. ||232||
whatever it is, it is worthwhile to speak with the Holy. ||232||
divine discourse with the saints, whatever is done, that is the net again. (Note: 1 ghari =24 minutes).

whoever holds converse with the saints — that is, asks questions and removes doubts through their words — for as long as one keeps their company and enjoys their words, that alone is the gain of this birth. ||232||
3Q5G: Bhaang = bhang, cannabis. Maachhulee = fish. Suraa = liquor. Paan = drinking. Paani = one who drinks (as 'dhan' gives 'dhani' = one with wealth, 'gun' gives 'guni' = one with virtue). The prose order of the whole line above is: "jo jo suraapaan praanee bhaang maachhulee khaanh". Khaanh = eat.

O Kabir! If people, after 'bhagtan setee goste', also go on pilgrimages and keep fasts and observances, and those drinkers also eat bhang and fish (that is, they go to the sangat too, and also eat and drink meat and liquor, and also commit vices),
Kabeer, those mortals who consume marijuana, fish and wine
Kabir, whosoever of the mortals partake of meat, fish and wine.
Sri Kabir ji says: the (bhaang) flesh of fish and the like, and (suraa) wine, that is, liquor — whoever eats and (paan) drinks these things —
YACT: Te sabhai = all of those (pilgrimages, fasts, observances and the like). Rasaatal jaanh = go to ruin, bring not the least gain. ||233||
then all their deeds of pilgrimage, fasting and the like go entirely to waste. ||233||
- no matter what pilgrimages, fasts and rituals they follow, they will all go to hell. ||233||
Whatever pilgrimages, fasting and daily rites they may perform, they all go to hell.

even though they have done good deeds such as pilgrimages, fasts and observances, still they go (sabhai rasaatal) to hell; meaning, they do not attain the high state of liberation, and keep wandering in the 8.4 million. ||233|| ☬ He shows his own resolve:
NGZG: Loin = eyes. Kar rahau = I keep. Saajan = the beloved Husband-Prabhu. Ghat maah le = keeping safe in the heart.

(O my friend of the sangat! Since I gained 'saadhoo sang', I hold only 'bhagtan setee goste'; through the blessing of this 'saadhoo sang',) keeping the beloved Husband-Prabhu safe in my heart, I keep my eyes lowered (from vices such as 'bhaang maachhulee suraa'),
Kabeer, I keep my eyes lowered, and enshrine my Friend within my heart.
I keep my eyes down and enshrine my friend within my mind.
Taking the Friend, Parmeshvar, into the (ghat) heart, I keep my eyes lowered from looking at anyone else.
NQSV: Peea sau = with the beloved Prabhu. Khelau = I play. Lakhaavau naahi = I do not tell. ||234||
(instead of playing games with these pleasures of the world) I enjoy all delights with the Husband-Prabhu; but I tell (this secret) to no one. ||234||
I enjoy all pleasures with my Beloved, but I do not let anyone else know. ||234||
I enjoy every pleasure with my Beloved and disclose it to none.
With all delights I play — that is, enjoy — with that Husband, and reveal it to no one. ||234||
LZ13: Jaam = pahir, a watch of three hours. Aath jaam = eight watches (Note: day and night together have eight watches), day and night, at every moment. Chausath ghari = sixty-four gharis (Note: a watch has eight gharis; sixty-four gharis make the eight watches, day and night, every moment). Tua = (Sanskrit tvaam) You. Nirkhat rahai = keeps gazing. Jeeu = my soul.
(O friend! I say only to the Husband-Prabhu: "O Husband!) all eight watches, every ghari, my soul keeps gazing only at You."
Twenty-four hours a day, every hour, my soul continues to look to You, O Lord.
For the eight watches and sixty-four gharis of time (all the time), my soul continues to look towards You, O Lord.
"O Husband! All eight watches and sixty-four gharis may my soul keep looking only at You."
ZU0W: Neeche ... karau = why should I lower my eyes from any being? I now hate no being. ||235||
(O friend!) I see the Husband-Prabhu alone in all bodies; so I hate no living being at all. ||235||
Why should I keep my eyes lowered? I see my Beloved in every heart. ||235||
Why should I cast down my eyes, since I see my Beloved in every heart?
So why should I lower my eyes, when in all (ghat) bodies, O Husband, I see You alone pervading? ||235||
S7UM: Sun sakhee = O my friend, listen. Peea mah = in the beloved Husband-Prabhu. Jeeu = soul. Jeea mah = in the soul. Ki = or.

O friend! (Through the blessing of 'saadhoo sang' a wondrous play has come about within me; I can no longer tell whether) my soul lives in the Husband-Prabhu, or the Beloved has come to live in my soul.
Listen, O my companions: my soul dwells in my Beloved, and my Beloved dwells in my soul.
Hear! O my mate, my soul abides in my Love, or rather my Lord abides in my soul.
O saintly friends! Does the Husband, Ishvar, live in the soul, (ki) or does the soul live in the Husband, Ishvar? ☬ Answer:
KBEH: Boojhau nahee = O friend, you cannot understand. ||236||
O friend! You cannot now understand whether within me there is my soul or my beloved Husband-Prabhu. ||236||
I realize that there is no difference between my soul and my Beloved; I cannot tell whether my soul or my Beloved dwells in my heart. ||236||
Now I realise that there is no difference between my soul and my Love. Hence, I can say not, whether my soul abides in my heart or my Lord.

Then the saints say: O friend! You do not understand the nature of the soul and the Husband, which is this: in this very (ghat) body, the one qualified by the inner faculty is the jiva, and the witness that is only reflected in the inner faculty is Ishvar; in reality both are of one single nature. ||236||
5QEE: But, O Kabir! (Say: the gift of this life that I have received came from the True Guru, the giver of life, who is Himself a lover of the Name; giving the sacred thread and the like, and showing the path of ritual,) the Brahmin can be called the guru only of worldly people; the Brahmin cannot become the giver of teaching to those who do devotion,
Kabeer, the Brahmin may be the guru of the world, but he is not the Guru of the devotees.
Kabir, the Brahman may be the Guru of the world, however, he is not the Guru of the saints.
Though the Brahmin is the guru of the whole world — that is, worthy of worship — still he is not the guru of the devotees.
V6B7: Arajh = getting caught. Urajh = getting entangled. Pach = being ruined. Mooa = has died, died a spiritual death; their soul could not live the life of union with Prabhu. ||237||

because he himself, thinking over and over the entanglements of the rituals of the four Vedas, such as sacrifices, has worn himself out in them and died a spiritual death (his own soul could not enjoy the bliss of union with Prabhu; how can he bring the devotees that taste?) ||237||
He rots and dies in the perplexities of the four Vedas. ||237||
He rots to death in the perplexities of the four Vedas.
For in the four Vedas — or, pondering the Vedas — he (arajh urajh) wore himself out in the fire of ego and (pach) burned to death. ||237||
L60K: Ret mah = in the sand (Note: the word 'ret' always ends in aunkar (u), and in this way it is feminine. This final (u) of the word stays even with a postposition). Haathee = by an elephant.
Parmatma's Name is, as it were, sugar scattered in sand; this sugar cannot be picked out of the sand by an elephant.
The Lord is like sugar, scattered in the sand; the elephant cannot pick it up.
God is like sugar, scattered in the sand. An elephant can not pick it up.

The sugar that is Hari, the Name, lies (bikhree) scattered in the sand of the world; that sugar (haathee) by the hands [sic: the verb seems to have dropped out; likely "cannot be picked"] — that is, by gross actions such as sacrifices; meaning, by being egoistic, Brahm is not attained.
YBRN: Kahi = says. Gur = the Guru. Bhalee bujhaaee = has given good understanding. Keetee = ant. Hoi kai = becoming. Khaai = can eat. ||238||
Kabir says: the perfect True Guru alone has given this good understanding, that a person can eat this sugar by becoming an ant. ||238||
Says Kabeer, the Guru has given me this sublime understanding: become an ant, and feed on it. ||238||
Says Kabir, the Guru has given me this sublime secret; that is to become like an ant and then partake of it.
Sri Kabir ji says: the True Guru has shown me a good way. What? Becoming like an ant — that is, with humility, or with an awareness turned towards the self — eat it; meaning, know it. ||238||
1MXZ: Tuhi = to you. Saadh = longing, yearning, desire. Piramm = love. Goi = ball.

O Kabir! If you long to play the game of Prabhu's love, then cut off your head and make it a ball (remove your ego in such a way that, even if people kick you, so be it: 'Kabir, become a pebble on the path, giving up the pride of the mind').
Kabeer, if you desire to play the game of love with the Lord, then cut off your head, and make it into a ball.
Kabir, if you desire to play the game of the Lord's love, then, cut off you, your head and make it into a ball.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother! If you have the (saadh) faith to attain Parmeshvar, the (piramm) Husband, then cut off your head and make it a (goi) ball; meaning, become free of ego.
EMCG: Haal kar = become intoxicated (Note: the Naushahi fakirs play 'haal' and become intoxicated). Ta hoi = let it be. ||239||
Playing this game, become so intoxicated that whatever (treatment the world gives you) happens, let it happen. ||239||
Lose yourself in the play of it, and then whatever will be, will be. ||239||
Playing, and playing, be you lost in it and then let happen what happen.
Playing this game of devotion, become joyful and know this: whatever is to happen will happen; meaning, become free of worry about worldly dealings. ||239||
G6SD: Paake setee = with the ripe (Guru), by taking refuge in the perfect True Guru.
But, O Kabir! If you long to play this game of Prabhu's love, then play it by taking refuge in the perfect True Guru (the ritualist Brahmin does not have this thing).
Kabeer, if you desire to play the game of love with the Lord, play it with someone with committment.
Kabir, if you desire your Beloved, then play you with the True Guru.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother! If you have (saadh) faith in that (piramm) Husband, then play with the saints who are ripe in knowledge; meaning, keep the company of those saints.
6MSG: Crushing unripe mustard yields neither oil nor oil-cake (such is the state of the unripe gurus made by giving the sacred thread and the like). ||240||
Pressing the unripe mustard seeds produces neither oil nor flour. ||240||
Pressing of the unripe mustard yields neither oil-cake nor oil.

For those who are worn out (pel) crushing unripe mustard gain neither oil-cake nor oil. The meaning is this: those who have kept bad company find no happiness in this world or the next. ||240|| ☬ Here is the testimony of Namdev ji:
WKVN: Dolahi = waver, wander, grope. Gat = state, condition. Andh gat = as is the state of the blind, like the blind. Ar = and. Cheenhat naahee = (Note: under the letter 'n' there is a half 'h') do not recognise.
The people who search (for Prabhu) but cannot recognise the devotees grope about just like the blind.
Searching, the mortal stumbles like a blind person, and does not recognize the Saint.
Searching for God, man stumbles like the blind one and recognises not the saints.
Through ignorance these beings go searching like the (gat) state of the blind, and do not know the saints to be the ones who bring the attainment of Parmeshvar.
74H7: Kahi = says. Kiu paaeeai = cannot be found. Bin bhagtahu = without (the company of) those who do devotion. Bhagvant = Bhagvan, Parmatma. ||241||
Namdev says: without (the company of) the people who do devotion, Bhagvan cannot be found. ||241||
Says Naam Dayv, how can one obtain the Lord God, without His devotee? ||241||
Says Nam Dev, how can one obtain the Illustrious Lord without His saint?
Sri Namdev ji says: O brother! Without meeting the devotees, how can Bhagvant be found? The meaning is this: Bhagvant is found only by meeting the devotees. ||241|| ☬ The testimony of Ravidas ji:
N0LY: So = like. Karahi = do. Aan = other and other.
(All comforts lie in the remembrance of Prabhu, but) the people who leave the diamond of Parmatma's Name and hope for comforts from other and other places,
Forsaking the Diamond of the Lord, the mortals put their hopes in another.
Forsaking the jewel-like God, they who pin their hope on another.
Those who leave that diamond which is Hari and hope in another —
ZHVD: Dojak = hell; the place where beings must suffer nothing but pain. Jaahige = (that is,) go, fall. Dojak jaahige = fall into hells, suffer nothing but pain. Sat = true, the right thing. Bhaakhai = says. ||242||
those people always suffer only pain; Ravidas tells this true thing. ||242||
Those people shall go to hell; Ravi Daas speaks the Truth. ||242||
Those persons shall go to hell, truly, says Rav Dass.
those people will go to hell. Sri Ravidas Bhagat ji utters a true word. ||242||
SLNR: Jau = if. Grihu karahi = you make a home, you become a householder. Ta = then. Dharam = duty, the duty of a householder. Bairaag = renunciation.

O Kabir! If you become a householder, then also carry out the duty of a householder (that is, remember Prabhu, keep yourself from vices, and hate no one; but living in the household) if you are going to stay sunk in Maya, then it is better to renounce it.
Kabeer, if you live the householder's life, then practice righteousness; otherwise, you might as well retire from the world.
Kabir, if you are embracing a domestic life, practise righteousness; otherwise renounce the world.
Sri Kabir ji says: O being! If you live as a householder, then turn the mind towards dharma; otherwise take up renunciation.
AJNP: The person who becomes a renunciant and then still gathers the entanglement of Maya along with it — know that as their great misfortune (they are fit for no place). ||243||
If someone renounces the world, and then gets involved in worldly entanglements, he shall suffer terrible misfortune. ||243||
If the world-renouncer is involved in worldly entanglements; great is his misfortune.

The person who becomes a renunciant, abandons the household, and then again does deeds that bind — that is, gets caught in worldly activity — their fortune is very poor. The meaning is: whoever, having withdrawn, gets caught again in worldly activity is unfortunate. ||243||
EFEY: The saloks of Sheikh Farid ji.

Farid ji was born into the Sheikh community. For a time early on he committed acts such as theft; then, becoming detached and leaving the world, he met a pir at Ajmer and attained the state of a saint. Then Farid ji, travelling through the lands, uttered saloks that point to detachment. Most of them he spoke at Pakpattan, which is his place; others he spoke here and there. Taking the soul as the bride and Yama as the husband, Sri Farid ji says:
1CL5: Akal Purakh is One, and is found through the True Guru's grace.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but one God. By the True Guru's grace, is He obtained.
AGC0: Jit = in which. Jit dihaarai = on which day. Dhan = bride. Varee = will be chosen, will be married. Saahe = (her) appointed time.
The day on which the (soul-)bride will be married — that time has been written (in advance) (that is, even before the being comes into the world, the time of its death is fixed),
The day of the bride's wedding is pre-ordained.
On the day, the women enters into the body, the time of her wedding is writ.
On the day this soul — the subtle body of eight parts — (varee) entered this body, from that very day it had written for it (saahe) the union with Yama, its husband.
K78Q: the angel of death, whom one had only heard of with one's ears, comes and shows his face (that is, the one heard of before at the deaths of others now comes and shows his face to the soul-bride whose turn has come).
On that day, the Messenger of Death, of whom she had only heard, comes and shows its face.
On the day of wedding, the myrmidon of death, of whom she had heard with her ears, comes and shows his face.
So its (malak) master, the husband, Yama, who is heard of with the ears, will come and show his face.
FA4Z: Breaking the bones again and again (that is, weakening the body with disease and the like), the poor soul is drawn out (of it).
It breaks the bones of the body and pulls the helpless soul out.
Breaking the bones, the poor soul is taken out of the body.
At that time the (nimaanee) poor, helpless soul will be pulled out of the body, the bones being broken and shattered.
0NJJ: Na chalnee = cannot be put off. Jindu koon = to the soul.
Make the soul understand (this): this fixed time (of death) cannot be put off.
That pre-ordained time of marriage cannot be avoided. Explain this to your soul.
The recorded time of marriage cannot the altered. Explain you this to your soul.
So the appointed times written as the measure of the breaths are not moved — that is, they do not go away. Therefore, O brother, make this soul understand, so that it becomes devoted to worship.
H9GJ: Maran = death. Var = bridegroom. Parnaai = having married.
The soul is, as it were, the bride; death (the angel of death) is (her) bridegroom; he will surely marry (the soul) and take her away,
The soul is the bride, and death is the groom. He will marry her and take her away.
The soul is the bride and death her Groom. he will marry her and take her away.
Then Yama, the (maran) killer of people, the (var) husband, will (parnaai) marry the soul-bride and take her away.
1PX8: Jol kai = having sent off. Kai gal = on whose neck? Dhaai = running.
Having sent off (the soul) with its own hands, on whose neck will this (body) fall? (that is, it will be left without support).
After the body sends her away with its own hands, whose neck will it embrace?
Sending her with its own hands, whose neck shall the body run to embrace?
At that time, having (jol) set off, on whose neck will she throw her arms and cling? That is, at that time Yama's messenger will not let her meet anyone.
Q69L: Vaalahu = than a hair. Pursalaat = pul siraat, the bridge of Sirat. Kannee = with the ears.
O Farid! Have you never heard the name of the 'bridge of Sirat', which is finer even than a hair?
The bridge to hell is narrower than a hair; haven't you heard of it with your ears?
Finer than even a hair is the bridge of hell. Have you not heard of it with yours ears?
So, O brother, the (pursalaat) bridge on Yama's road — its edge is finer even than a hair; you have not heard of its pain with your ears.
LU3C: Kirree pavandeeee = while calls are being made. Kirree = call. Aap = yourself. Na muhaai = do not cheat, do not deceive, do not let yourself be robbed. ||1||

Even while the calls are reaching your ears, do not let yourself be robbed (that is, the world is an ocean in which waves of vice are rising; to cross it safe and sound, 'darveshi' is, as it were, a bridge, very narrow and fine — that is, living as a darvesh is very hard, but it is the only way to be saved from the vices of the world. Through the scriptures the Gurus and prophets are calling out to you to be saved from the danger of the waves of vice; listen carefully, and do not waste your life in vain). ||1||
Fareed, the call has come; be careful now - don't let yourself be robbed. ||1||
Farid! The call is about to come, beware and do not get robbed.

Sri Farid ji says: so, O brother, (kirree pavandeeee) while the calls are being made — that is, while the Vedas and Shastras are calling out — do not stand there and (muhaai) hide yourself; meaning, make an effort in worshipping Vahiguru. ||1|| ☬ Once, going along the road, Farid ji saw melons and asked for some. When the owner of the field did not give them, at that moment the thought of farming arose in his mind; turning it back, Sri Farid ji says:
9RH3: Gaakhree = hard. Darvesee = the life of a fakir. Dar = of the door (of Parmatma). Bhat = like.
O Farid! Being a fakir at the door (of Parmatma) is a hard (task), and I am walking just like worldly people;
Fareed, it is so difficult to become a humble Saint at the Lord's Door.
Farid! Difficult, is the saintship of the Lord's door. May I therefore walk in the way of the world?
O mind! Being a (darveshi) fakir at the door of Parmeshvar is (gaakhree) hard; so should I give up being a darvesh and walk again (bhat) like the world — that is, take up farming?

DJ5E: Kijh = anything at all. Bujhai = is understood, is known. Dunia = attachment to the world. Gujhee = hidden. Bhaah = fire.

The world (looks like a garden, but attachment to it is in truth) a hidden fire (which keeps smouldering within the mind; the beings caught in it get) no sense or understanding (of the right path of life).
I know nothing; I understand nothing. The world is a smouldering fire.
I see nothing and know nothing, as the world is a smoldering fire.
This world has no understanding of dharma and no awareness of its own true nature. That is why the whole world is caught in the hidden fire of hope and craving.
ZZ0A: Saanee merai = my Master. Hambhee = I too. Dajhaan aah = would have burned. ||3||

My Master has shown me grace (and saved me from it); otherwise (like other people) I too would have burned (in it) (that is, Prabhu Himself, by His grace, saves us from attachment to Maya; it is not in our own power to take this 'bundle' off our heads and throw it away). ||3||
My Lord did well to warn me about it; otherwise, I would have been burnt as well. ||3||
My Lord did well to warn me, otherwise, I too would have been burnt.

So my Master has done well by me, in saving me from this household life; otherwise I too would have been (dajhaan) burned in this fire in the same way. ||3|| ☬ Having said this, Farid ji told the owner of the field: "Go; your melons will become as they were." Then he asked: "What wonder is this?" Farid ji said: "One head will be left in that field; it will give you the answer." Hearing this, when he came and looked, all had become melons again. He asked the one head that lay there; it both laughed and wept. He asked it the reason for laughing and weeping, and the head said: "O unfortunate man! Wandering through the 8.4 million, we had now come into this birth. If even one of us had been of use to that saint, we would all have been liberated. That is why I laughed. But you did not grant the saint's request. Because we were of no use to him, we are left in the 8.4 million again; that is why I wept." Hearing such words from that head, that householder too became detached and began to worship.
7ZR8: Til = (that is,) breaths. Thorrre = very few. Sammal = carefully, thoughtfully.
O Farid! If I knew that there are very few sesame seeds (of breath, in this vessel of the body), I would fill my handful carefully (that is, I would not let the breaths of life pass carelessly).
Fareed, if I had known that I had so few sesame seeds, I would have been more careful with them in my hands.
Farid! If I had known that the breaths in my procession are so few, I would have carefully filled my handfuls.

If I had known that the sesame seeds of breath are few — that is, numbered — I would have filled my handful with care; meaning, I would have used the breaths carefully, that is, spent them in worship. Or: if I had known that the sesame — that is, things — are few, that is, trifling, I would have filled my handful — that is, taken them — with care.
6B1W: Sahu = the Husband-Prabhu. Nandhrra = a little child, (that is, of a childlike nature). ||4||
If I came to understand that (my) Husband (Prabhu) has a childlike nature (that is, loves an innocent nature), then I too would give up pride (in this bundle of the world). ||4||
If I had known that my Husband Lord was so young and innocent, I would not have been so arrogant. ||4||
If I had known, that my spouse was so young, then, I would have taken less pride.

And if I had known that sahu — that is, youth — is trifling, I would have taken little pride in youth; or, if I had known that Parmeshvar the Husband is met by (nandhrra) becoming lowly, I would have taken little pride — that is, no pride at all. ||4||
QPM6: Larr = hem. Chhijnaa = will tear. Peerree = firm.
(O Husband-Prabhu!) If I understood that (because of this 'bundle') the hem (of Yours that I hold) wears through (that is, distance comes between us), then I would tie a firm knot (to Your hem).
If I had known that my robe would come loose, I would have tied a tighter knot.
If I had knows that my skirt would be broken loose, I would have put a fast knot.

If I had known that the (larr) hem of the body would (chhijnaa) perish, I would have pulled it (peerree) tight and tied a knot; meaning, I would have put the body to worship, that is, made union with Hari the Husband.
THF1: Tai jevad = as great as You. Handh = having wandered. ||5||
(O Master!) I have wandered and looked through the whole world; I have found no other (companion) like You. ||5||
I have found none as great as You, Lord; I have looked and searched throughout the world. ||5||
As great as You, O Lord, I have found none. I have seen and searched the whole world.
I have (handh) wandered through the whole world and looked; no beloved as great as that Husband appears to me. ||5||
K95Q: Akal lateef = of subtle intellect, of fine understanding. Kaale lekh = the account of black deeds, scrutiny of others' bad deeds.
O Farid! If you are of fine intellect (wise), then do not scrutinise the bad deeds of other people;
Fareed, if you have a keen understanding, then do not write black marks against anyone else.
Farid! If you have keen understanding, then do not black write against others.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! If you are of (lateef) clever or pure intellect, then do not write black records — that is, do not commit sins.
TK0T: Gireevaan = the fold of one's garment at the chest. ||6||
put your face into the fold of your own garment and look (at how your own deeds are). ||6||
Look underneath your own collar instead. ||6||
Bend your head and look beneath your own collar.

Lowering the head of ego into the (gireevaan) robe of your own mind or body — or, with an inward-turned awareness — see God. ||6|| ☬ Once, going along the road, Farid ji sat down. Some men had eaten melons there and gone on. On the way their knife fell, so they came back there. They asked Farid ji about the knife; he said: "I have not seen it." Then those wicked men beat him with their hands and went away. After them, he makes his own mind understand:
BQUR: Tai = you. Tinha = (under the letter 'n' there is a half 'h'). Maare = maar. Na maare = do not strike. Ghumm = turning around, in return.
O Farid! Those (people) who strike you with fists (that is, cause you any pain) — do not turn and strike them back (that is, do not take revenge; rather),
Fareed, do not turn around and strike those who strike you with their fists.
Farid! To those who beat you with fists; do not return them beating turning around.
Sri Farid ji says: O mind! Those who strike you with fists — do not (ghumm) turn and strike them.
VC2K: Aapnarrai ghar = in your own home, in your own true self, in a state of peace. Chumm = having kissed. Jaaeeai = one reaches. ||7||
kissing their feet, one stays settled in one's own home (in a state of peace). ||7||
Kiss their feet, and return to your own home. ||7||
Kiss you their feet and go to your own house.

So let us kiss their feet and go to our own home. Or: the desires that have struck you birth after birth have not yet (mukeeaan) ended — that is, have not gone away. So now, turning inward, you do not strike them; meaning, strike down desire. By kissing the feet of the saints who have struck down their desires, one attains the home of one's true self. ||7||
7J2M: Tau = your. Khatan vel = the time to earn. Rata = dyed, absorbed, intoxicated. Siu = with.
O Farid! When it was the time for you to earn (the true earnings), then you stayed intoxicated with the world (its 'bundle').
Fareed, when there was time for you to earn good karma, you were in love with the world instead.
Farid! When there is time to earn salvation, then you are in love with the world.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! When it was your time to earn — that is, when you were in youth, able to do chanting, austerity and the like — then you were dyed in (dunee) Maya.
PTK5: Marg (printed 'maarag') = death. Savaaee = kept growing, kept becoming firmer. Jaan = when. Bharia = (the measure) was filled, the breaths were completed. Neehi = (under the letter 'n' there is a half 'h'), foundation. ||8||
(In this way) the foundation of death kept growing firmer (that is, the time of death kept coming nearer); when all the breaths were completed, one had to depart from here. ||8||
Now, death has a strong foothold; when the load is full, it is taken away. ||8||
Death's foundation is strong, when the cup of breaths is filled, then, the soul is loaded oft.

The (neehi) foundation of (marg) death (savaaee) has stood through the whole life, or keeps growing — that is, the day of death comes near. Jaan bharia — that is, when the last breath was completed — at that very moment this being goes off, loaded with good and bad deeds. ||8||
S8XP: Theea = has happened. Ju = whatever. Bhoor = white.
O Farid! See what has happened (so far): the beard has turned white,
See, Fareed, what has happened: your beard has become grey.
See O Farid! What has happened? Your beard had grown grey.
Sri Farid ji says: O being! See what has happened: the beard too has turned grey; meaning, old age has now come to you.
A46J: Agahu = from the front. Pichha = the back, when you were born. ||9||
the time is drawing near from the side of death, and the back (when you were born) has been left far (behind) (so now stop doing childish things, and earn in preparation for what lies ahead). ||9||
That which is coming is near, and the past is left far behind. ||9||
Therefore, the future is near and the past is left far behind.
So now the day of death ahead has come near, and the day of birth has been left far behind. ||9||
CTJ4: Ji theea = whatever has happened. Sakar = sweet things. Vis = poison, painful.

O Farid! See what has happened (so far): (because the 'beard has turned white') even the sweet things of the world seem painful (because now, with the bodily senses weakened, one cannot enjoy those pleasures fully).
See, Fareed, what has happened: sugar has become poison.
See O Farid! What has happened? The sugar has become poison.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! See what has happened: the array of pleasures that in youth seemed like sugar — that is, sweet — now appears like poison, that is, painful.
KVHW: To whom but our own Master can we tell this sorrow? (that is, no one can stop this change, which happens according to Prabhu's laws). ||10||
Without my Lord, who can I tell of my sorrow? ||10||
Without my Lord, to whom should I tell my sorrow?
So now, apart from our own (saanee) Parmeshvar, to whom else should we tell our (vedan) pain? ||10||
090F: Pateeneeaan = have grown weak, have sunk down. Reene = empty, deaf.

O Farid! (The reason 'sugar' has become 'poison' is this:) the eyes, from seeing (the world's shows and spectacles), have (now) grown weak (the world's shows are still there as before, but the eyes no longer have the strength to see); the ears, from hearing and hearing (the world's songs and amusements), have (now) gone deaf.
Fareed, my eyes have become weak, and my ears have become hard of hearing.
Seeing my eyes have become week and hearing, and haring my ears have become deaf.
Sri Farid ji says: the eyes, from looking and looking at beauty, have grown (pateeneeaan) thin — that is, lost their sight; and the ears, from hearing talk, have become (reene) empty — that is, deaf.
831W: Saakh = branch, body. Pakandee aaeeaa = has ripened. Vann = colour. ||11||
(Not only the eyes and ears — the whole) body has grown old; it has changed to another colour altogether (it is no longer able to enjoy pleasures, and there is no cure for this sorrow). ||11||
The body's crop has become ripe and turned color. ||11||
The crop of the body has become ripe and has assumed another colour.
And the (saakh) crop of the body keeps ripening, for it has taken on another (vann) colour; meaning, in old age the body grew bent and the hair turned white. ||11||
7Z98: Kaalee = when the hair was black, while one had black hair. Raavia = enjoyed. Dhaulee = when the grey hair came. Koi = some rare one.
O Farid! Of those who did not love the Husband-Prabhu while their hair was black, only some rare one can remember God when the grey hair comes (that is, in old age).
Fareed, those who did not enjoy their Spouse when their hair was black - hardly any of them enjoy Him when their hair turns grey.
Farid! They, who enjoy not their spouse, when their hair are black; never enjoy Him, when their hair are grey.

Sri Farid ji says: O brother! Those who did not enjoy Vahiguru in the time of black hair — that is, in youth — that is, did not become one with Him through chanting: (koi) who among such people enjoys — that is, chants — in the time of (dhaulee) white hair?
Y7R2: Pirharree = love. Navela = new. Rang = love. ||12||
(O Farid!) Love the Master-Prabhu; (this) love will stay (ever) new (the love of the world's 'bundle' will break when the 'branch' of the body ripens). ||12||
So be in love with the Lord, so that your color may ever be new. ||12||
Love your Lord, that you may have fresh colour.
So, O brother, form (pirharree) love with Parmeshvar, the (saanee) Master of all; by forming that love you will gain a (navela) new colour of bliss. ||12||
4T54: Chit = in the mind. Chit kare = keeps in the mind, worships.
O Farid! If a person worships, the Master (can be found) both in youth and in old age.
Fareed, whether one's hair is black or grey, our Lord and Master is always here if one remembers Him.
Farid! Whether one's hair is black or grey, the Lord is ever there, if anyone remembers Him.

Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji, giving trust in Vahiguru to the minds of the old, utters through Farid ji: (kaalee dhaulee) in youth and in old age the Master is always found, if someone keeps Him in mind — that is, remembers Him with love. But that remembrance does not happen without love.
P5LC: Piram = love. Sabh koi = every being.
But let anyone try with longing: 'this love' cannot be attached by one's own attaching.
This loving devotion to the Lord does not come by one's own efforts, even though all may long for it.
By one's embracing, the love for the Lord is embraced not, even though, all may long for it.
Even if everyone (lochai) wishes to attach love, still love attached by one's own effort does not take hold in Him.
H2RB: Jai = to whomever. Tai = to that one. ||13||
This cup of love belongs to the Master (Himself); He gives it to whomever He pleases. ||13||
This cup of loving devotion belongs to our Lord and Master; He gives it to whomever He likes. ||13||
This cup of love belongs to the Lord. He given it to him whom He likes.

But this cup of love belongs to that Master, Vahiguru; He gives it to whomever He pleases. The meaning is: this love too is gained only as Hari's gift. ||13|| ☬ A courtesan's maid handed her the stick for applying kohl; when she applied it, it grated in her eyes. Seeing her in this state, Sri Farid ji utters:
S0VU: O Farid! (The being intoxicated in this 'hidden fire' — a garden to look at, but in truth fire — understands nothing, and keeps taking pride. But pride in what?) The (beautiful) eyes that had enchanted the world — I have seen those eyes too:
Fareed, those eyes which have enticed the world - I have seen those eyes.
Farid! The eyes, which charmed the world; those eyes I have seen.
The eyes that had enchanted the beings of the world — today I have seen those eyes come to this.
ZTRW: Sooi = chicks. Bahith = place to sit. ||14||

(at first they were so delicate that) they could not bear the line of kohl; then they became a nest for birds' chicks (that is, before our eyes bodily beauty is in the end destroyed; pride in it is false). ||14||
Once, they could not endure even a bit of mascara; now, the birds hatch their young in them! ||14||
They could endure not the streak of collyrium, but now the birds have hatched their young in them.
For those that could not bear a thick line of kohl — in them today birds' (sooi) chicks are sitting; meaning, in the end this was their state. ||14||
C8J3: Saitaan = Satan (that is, the mind) (Farid ji, following Islamic thought, calls Satan the instigator of evil). Kookedia chaangedia = even after explaining by calling out again and again.
O Farid! (However much) we call out and say it, (however much) we give counsel every day —
Fareed, they shouted and yelled, and constantly gave good advice.
Farid! The saints shout, shriek and give good advice always.
Sri Farid ji says: even while the Vedas are (kookendia) teaching, and the Shastras (chaangedia) calling out, and the True Guru is giving counsel every day —
SKER: Se = those people. Vannjaaia = has spoiled. ||15||
yet the people whom the Satan (of the mind) has spoiled — how can they turn their mind (away from the 'world')? ||15||
But those whom the devil has spoiled - how can they turn their consciousness towards God? ||15||
They whom the devil has spoiled, who can they turn their mind towards God?
the people whose mind Satan has led astray — how can they turn their mind towards Hari? That is, they do not turn it. ||15||
D7V0: Theeu = become. Pavaahee = of the path, of the road. Dabh = kusha grass, grass.
O Farid! Become (like) the grass on the path,
Fareed, become the grass on the path,
Farid! You become the spear grass of the path way,
Sri Farid ji says: be like the grass on the path; meaning, become the dust of everyone's feet.
SD3N: Je lorrahi = if you seek. Sabh = everywhere, in everything.
if you seek the Master (Prabhu) everywhere (that is, wish to see Him).
if you long for the Lord of all.
if you long for the Lord of all.
O brother! If you (lorrahi) wish to see the Master as wholly present in everything —
0M2G: Ik = one, some grass plant. Chhijahi = (people) break. Bia = many others (grass plants). Lataarreeahi = are trampled.
(People) break one plant (of grass), and many other plants are trampled (under their feet).
One will cut you down, and another will trample you underfoot;
When one breaks you and another tramples on you,
one may (chhijahi) break your limbs and another may trample you; meaning, even if someone gives you pain, you should forgive and stay patient.
