(If you make your nature like this,) then you will be accepted at the Master's door. ||16||
then, you shall enter the Court of the Lord. ||16||
then alone shall you enter the Lord's Court.
Then you will be let in at the Master's door; meaning, then you will attain the very form of Vahiguru. ||16||
N62M: Khaak = earth (this word always ends in aunkar (u); other such words are khand, vis, jind. When a postposition is used with these (u)-ending words, or they are used in some case-form, the (u) becomes (oo), as 'khaak' gives 'khaakoo', 'jind' gives 'jindoo', 'vis' gives 'visoo'). Jed = as great as, like.
O Farid! One should not speak ill of earth; nothing can equal earth.
Fareed, do not slander the dust; noting is as great as dust.
Farid! Slander not the dust; nothing is so great as dust.

Sri Farid ji says: do not slander the saints who hold humility like earth, for there is no one like them. For while living they stay in humility, and then they become the crown of all, worthy of everyone's worship.
139P: (While a person) lives, it is under their feet; (but when the person) dies, it comes to be on top of them (in the same way, a 'humble nature' cannot be matched: a person of humble nature may bear everyone's excesses in life, but by having subdued the mind they are the highest of all in spiritual state). ||17||
When we are alive, it is under our feet, and when we are dead, it is above us. ||17||
When man is alive, it is under his feet and when he is dead, it is over him.

Or: do not slander the visible earth, for there is nothing like this earth. While one is living it comes under the feet, and when one dies it is on top; meaning, the body is placed in the grave and earth is put over it. ||17||
0XGS: Nehu kia = what love? (that is, not real love). Koorra = false.
O Farid! If there is greed (for some worldly reward in return for worshipping God), then there is no real love (for God). (As long as) there is greed, the love is false.
Fareed, when there is greed, what love can there be? When there is greed, love is false.
Farid! When there is avarice, what love can there be then? If there is avarice, then false is the love.

Sri Farid ji says: when there is (lab) greed, what (nehu) love is there? That is, there is none; for if there is greed, love is false. Illustration: in the same way, as long as a seeker has a greed for sense-objects, there is no love for Parmeshvar; so if one is known to be greedy, their love is false.
Z9DZ: Kichar = how long? Jhat = time. Chhapar = on the thatched roof. Chhapar toote = on a broken thatched roof. Meh = rain. ||18||
How long can one pass the time under a broken thatched roof while the rain falls? (that is, when the worldly purpose is not fulfilled, the love will break). ||18||
How long can one remain in a thatched hut which leaks when it rains? ||18||
How long can one pass the time in a broken cottage in the rain?

Just as, while the clouds are raining, how much (jhat) time can be passed in a broken shelter? Only a little; in the end one must get wet. In the same way, with greed, love does not last for ever. ||18|| ☬ As Farid ji wandered in the forest, a voice came from the sky:
9PV6: Jangal jangal = every forest. Kia bhavahi = what is the gain in roaming? Van = in the forest. Kia morrehi = why do you trample?
O Farid! What is the gain in roaming every forest? Why do you go about trampling the thorns in the forest?
Fareed, why do you wander from jungle to jungle, crashing through the thorny trees?
Farid! Why wander you from forest to forest breaking down the thorns of the trees?
O Farid! Why do you wander from (jangal) wilderness to wilderness, (morrehi) trampling the forest thorns?
QV28: Vasee = lives. Hiaaleeai = in the heart. Kia dhoodhehi = what is the gain in searching? ||19||
God lives (in your) heart; what is the use of searching the forest? ||19||
The Lord abides in the heart; why are you looking for Him in the jungle? ||19||
The Lord abides in the heart, why then seek Him in the forest?
I, your (rab) Sustainer, am living in the house of your heart; so why do you (dhoodhehi) search outside in the forest? ||19||
U50Z: Inee jangheeai = with these legs. Doogar = hill, mountain. Bhavioomhi = I searched, I roamed (under the letter 'm' there is a half 'h').
O Farid! With these little legs (in youth) I used to roam over deserts and mountains,
Fareed, with these small legs, I crossed deserts and mountains.
Farid! With these small legs, I have traversed across deserts and mountains.
Sri Farid ji says: in youth, with these excellent (jangheeai) legs, I kept (bhavioomhi) wandering over sandy (thal) deserts and (doongar) mountains.
PEA4: Aj = (that is,) in old age. Fareedai theeom = has become to me, Farid. Koojrra = a small water pot. ||20||
but today (in old age) to me, Farid, (this) water pot (lying a little way off) has become a hundred kos away (so the time for worship too is youth, when the body can serve). ||20||
But today, Fareed, my water jug seems hundreds of miles away. ||20||
However, today, to Farid, his jug appears at a distance of hundreds of miles.

But today, in old age, even fetching the (koojrra) water pot has (theeomhi) become hundreds of kos away for me; meaning, in old age the body has grown weak. Or: through these subtle desires I kept wandering in high and low births; today, having become free of desire, the water pot of the body has become hundreds of kos away — that is, I have known myself as unattached to the body, or have become free of birth and death. ||20|| ☬ A carpenter named Jassa was Farid ji's friend. Once he came and stayed the night with Farid ji in the forest where he lived. At that time Farid ji had no food or clothing. Then, in the night of the month of Poh, the cold struck him and, from hunger, he could not sleep either. What that Jassa says, Farid ji utters in the salok:
GGFD: Dhukh uthan = smoulder, ache. Paas = the sides of the body. (It is necessary to see the difference between the words 'paas' and 'paas[i]'. See salok no. 45, 'paas damaame'. Grammatically 'paas' is a noun, plural, meaning the sides of the body, the ribs. 'Paas[i]' is a postposition, meaning with whom, near whom).
O Farid! In the long (winter) nights the sides (from lying and lying) begin to ache (in the same way, time does not pass while one waits on another's hope; sitting at another's door one grows weary).
Fareed, the nights are long, and my sides are aching in pain.
Farid! Long are the nights and the sides of my body ache and ache.
O Farid ji! The nights of the month of Poh are long, and my sides keep aching and aching.

3MAF: Viddaanee = another's. (In the words 'jinha' and 'tinha' there is an 'h' with the letter 'n'). Vaddeeaan = long. Dhrig = deserving of reproach. ||21||
So, those people who look to others in hope — their life is to be reproached (keep your hope in the One God). ||21||
Cursed are the lives of those who place their hopes in others. ||21||
Accursed is the life of those, whose hope rests on others.
Those who keep hoping in another — their life is accursed; meaning, hoping in you, I have stayed in pain. ||21|| ☬ Understanding his meaning, Farid ji answers:
9NFV: Vaaria hoda = had hidden. Mita aaeerriaan = from friends who have come.
O Farid! If I ever hide anything from friends who have come,
Fareed, if I had been there when my friend came, I would have made myself a sacrifice to him.
Farid! If I had been present, when my friend came, I would have sacrificed myself to him.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! If, when my friends came and it was with me, I (vaaria) held it back — that is, did not give it —
3YGF: Herra = body, flesh. Majeeth jiu = like madder. Jalai = burns. ||22||
then my body burns (like this) as madder on burning coals (that is, if the mind ever slips from serving a guest who has come to the house, the soul feels great pain). ||22||
Now my flesh is burning red on the hot coals. ||22||
Now my flesh burns like the madder on the burning coal.
then may my (herra) body burn like madder on the embers of fire; meaning, I have kept nothing hidden from you. ||22||
74EB: Bijaureeaan = of the Bijaur region (this region is in the Pathan country, beyond Malakand and Swat). Daakh = small grape. Kikar = kikar (acacia) saplings.
O Farid! (A person who hopes for a happy life without worship is like that farmer) who sows kikar saplings but wants (to eat) the small grapes of the Bijaur region (from those saplings),
Fareed, the farmer plants acacia trees, and wishes for grapes.
Farid! The farmer plants the tree of Acasia arabica and desires the grapes of Bijour.
Sri Farid ji says: as some farmer sows kikars and wants to get grapes of the land of Bijaur,
MN5R: Handhai = goes about. Paidha lorrai = wants to wear. ||23||
goes about (all of life) having wool spun, but wants to wear silk. ||23||
He is spinning wool, but he wishes to wear silk. ||23||
He goes about spinning wool, however, he wishes to wear silk.

(handhai) goes about having wool spun and wants to wear (pat) silk — so too the being, like a farmer, sows the kikars of bad deeds and wants the grapes of the land of Bijaur, the comforts of heaven; and again has the wool of desire-driven deeds spun, and wants to wear the silk of the happiness of attaining the true self. This is impossible. ||23|| ☬ When Farid ji first became detached, he did austerities in the forest for twelve years, living on fruit and flowers; for twelve years he hung in a well; and for twelve years he served Khwaja Pir at Ajmer. At last, to test him, the pir made the fire disappear. With a watch of the night left, Farid ji used to heat water and have the pir bathe. That day, finding no fire, he saw that his service would be obstructed. Saddened in mind he began to look about, and then he saw a lamp burning somewhere far off; it was raining and there was mud. At that time Sri Farid ji says, concerning his own mind:
YS8Y: O Farid! (Because of the rain) there is mud in the lane, (the Beloved's) house is far (from here), (but) (my) love for the Beloved is (great).
Fareed, the path is muddy, and the house of my Beloved is so far away.
Farid! The lanes are mud-ridden and the house of my Beloved, whom I love, is far away.
In the lanes there is mud, and the house with the lamp is far; but I also have (nehu) love in the service of my beloved, the pir.
TGJR: Rahaan = if I stay, (that is,) if I do not go. Ta = then. Tutai = breaks. Nehu = love. ||24||
If I go (to meet the Beloved), my blanket gets soaked; if I do not go (for fear of the rain and mud), my love breaks. ||24||
If I go out, my blanket will get soaked, but if I remain at home, then my heart will be broken. ||24||
If I go, then my blanket shall be drenched and if I remain at home, then, my love shall sever.
I have only one (kamblee) blanket on my body. If I go to that house to fetch fire, my blanket gets soaked in the rain; and if I do not go, my love for serving the pir ji breaks. ||24||
ME5P: Alah = by God's will, God willing. Bhijau = let it be soaked (Let it be soaked) (grammatically this word is 'imperative', third person, singular (Imperative mood, Third person, Singular number), so the word 'kamblee' cannot mean 'O blanket!'. Likewise 'varsau' too is 'imperative, third person, singular'; it means 'let it rain' (Let it rain). Here too the word 'moh' [sic: 'meh'] cannot mean 'O rain!', for grammatically the word 'meh' is plainly 'nominative, singular'. If it were 'vocative', it would not have (u) at the end. For further reflection: the word 'tutau' too is like the words 'bhijau sijau' and 'varsau'.
Let (my) blanket be soaked through and through; God willing, let the rain (too) keep pouring,
My blanket is soaked, drenched with the downpour of the Lord's Rain.
However, let my blanket be wetted and drenched with the down pour of the Lord's rain.
Sri Farid ji says: even if this blanket gets soaked and drenched — or the shawl gets soaked and some limb too gets (sijau) wet — Alah, let the (meh) rain keep pouring;
8PGG: (but) I will surely meet those friends, (so that) my love does not break. ||25||
I am going out to meet my Friend, so that my heart will not be broken. ||25||
I will go and meet that friend, so that my love may be severed not.

so, bringing fire and heating water, let me go and meet the pir ji, my friend, so that my love does not break. ☬ Having said this, Farid ji went to fetch fire. Ahead, there was fire in a courtesan's house. When he asked her for fire, she said: "Lie with me; or give me your eye; then I will give you fire." Farid ji did not agree to lie with her, and, taking out one of his eyes, gave it to her and brought back the fire. He heated water and had the pir ji bathe. Then the pir ji asked: "Why have you bound a bandage over your eye?" Farid ji said: "My eye is sore." The pir said: "Shall the eye become small or large?" He said: "Whatever is your will." The pir said: "One should not set oneself equal to God; so the eye will become small." Having said this, he had the bandage untied, and the eye became as it was. But it stayed smaller than the other. Seeing this, the pir said: "Now your service is complete; so go and sit somewhere and worship." Then Farid ji came and stayed at Pakpattan. Now one eye of his descendants stays small, and they are called Chishti. Now he gives a second meaning of these two saloks. ☬ Or: in the lanes of the senses there is the mud of the desires for sense-objects, and the Beloved, Hari, whom ...
E7NW: Mai = to me. Bholaava = misapprehension, illusion, worry, concern. Mat = lest. Mat hoi jaai = lest it become.
O Farid! I (keep) worrying about (my) turban, lest (my turban) get dirty (with earth),
Fareed, I was worried that my turban might become dirty.
Farid! I am worried about my turban lest it should be soiled.
Sri Farid ji says: in the minds of beings like us there is the illusion about the turban, lest my turban get dirty.
CZH3: but the foolish soul does not know that the earth eats up even the head. ||26||
My thoughtless self did not realize that one day, dust will consume my head as well. ||26||
However, my thoughtless soul is unaware that dust will eat my head too.

But this (rooh) being, (gahila) foolish or heedless, does not know that, lying in the grave, even the head will be eaten by the earth. ||26|| ☬ Knowing Parmeshvar's bliss to be greater than all tasty things, he prays:
7YZM: Nivaat = rock sugar. Khand = (this word always ends in (u); see salok no. 37). Maakhiu = {the letter 'o' of this word carries two vowel signs, (o) and (u); the true word, with (o), is 'maakhio', but here, to keep the metre's count, it is to be read 'maakhiu'} maakhio, honey.
O Farid! Raw sugar, refined sugar, rock sugar, jaggery, honey and buffalo milk —
Fareed: sugar cane, candy, sugar, molasses, honey and buffalo's milk
Farid! Unrefined sugar, loaf sugar, molasses, honey and buffalo's milk,
Sri Farid ji says: raw sugar and refined sugar, (nivaat) rock sugar, (maakhion) honey, buffalo milk and the like —
2CQU: Rab = O God! O Parmatma! Na pujan = do not reach. Tudh = You. ||27||
all these things are sweet. But, O God! (in sweetness these things) cannot reach (the sweetness of Your Name). ||27||
- all these things are sweet, but they are not equal to You. ||27||
all these things are sweet, however, O Lord, they equal You not.
all these things are sweet, but, O (rab) Vahiguru, they cannot come up to the taste of Your Name; meaning, the nectar of the Name is greater than all. ||27||
J9LB: Kaath kee rotee = bread dry as wood, plain coarse bread. Laavan = relish, curry.
O Farid! My bread is plain and coarse (that is, simple) (earned with my own hands); my hunger itself is the relish (with this bread).
Fareed, my bread is made of wood, and hunger is my appetizer.
Farid! My bread is the wooden-pot and the hunger is my cooked vegetable.
Farid ji says: my bread is of actual wood, and the (laavan) relish to eat with it is my hunger.
YL0Z: Those who eat rich food suffer great hardships (that is, the simple bread of one's own earning is good; cravings bring a person to ruin). ||28||
Those who eat buttered bread, will suffer in terrible pain. ||28||
They, who eat buttered bread, shall suffer great pain.
Those who have eaten buttered bread — that is, who have enjoyed sense-pleasures — will also bear (ghane) very many pains. ||28||
TXX2: O Farid! Eat the plain dry bread (of your own earning) and drink cold water.
Eat dry bread, and drink cold water.
Eat you the coarse dry bread and drink the cold water.
Farid ji says: O brother! Eating (rukhee sukhee) dry bread, drink cool water and stay happy.
RLGY: But do not make your mind crave on seeing another's tasty bread. ||29||
Fareed, if you see someone else's buttered bread, do not envy him for it. ||29||
Farid! Seeing another's buttered bread let not your mind long for it.

Seeing another's buttered bread — that is, seeing the comforts and pleasures of those driven by rajas — do not make your soul crave. ||29|| ☬ A holy man named Shah Sharaf was a man of knowledge, and did not keep fasts or offer namaz and the like. Then one day Farid ji missed his namaz. Then, reasoning with that saint, Sri Farid ji says to his disciple:
1YPS: Siu = with. Ang = body. Murr jaai = is breaking. Murre murr jaai = aches again and again, feels as if it were breaking.
(Only) today I did not sleep with my Beloved (that is, only today I was not absorbed in the beloved Husband-Parmatma, and now) it is as if my body were breaking.
This night, I did not sleep with my Husband Lord, and now my body is suffering in pain.
I slept not with my spouse during the night and every part of my body is pining in pain.
Today I have not slept with Parmeshvar, my Husband; meaning, today I have not been able to worship; because of that my (ang) heart keeps (murre murr) withering again and again.
441H: Dohaaganee = the deserted bride, separated from her husband, unfortunate, ill-fated. Jaai = going. Rain = night (that is, the whole night of life). ||30||

Go and ask the deserted (ill-fated) brides how (always) your night passes (that is, I forgot Prabhu only today for a little while and I am in pain; those who never remembered Him at all must pass their whole life in pain). ||30||
Go and ask the deserted bride, how she passes her night. ||30||
Go and ask you the deserted one, as to how does she passes her night.
So, O brother, go and ask this (dohaaganee) deserted bride: how do your days and nights pass without worship such as namaz? ||30||
4GL2: Saahurai = in the in-laws' home, in the next world, in Prabhu's presence. Dhoee = support, place. Peeeeai = in the parents' home, in this world.
That woman finds no place, no support, either in her in-laws' home or in her parents' home,
She finds no place of rest in her father-in-law's home, and no place in her parents' home either.
She finds no refuge in the house of her father-in-law and also no place in her parents.
Then that saint replies: in the (saahurai) next world you find no support, and in (peeeeai) this world you have no place; meaning, sometimes you hang in a well, sometimes you wander in the forest.
8M0H: Pir = the Husband-Prabhu. Vaatarree = even a little word. Dhan = bride. ||31||

the bride whom the Husband does not ask after even a little — let her call herself a happy wife if she likes (that is, beings who miss the remembrance of Prabhu are ruined in both this world and the next; an outward garb of worship cannot help). ||31||
Her Husband Lord does not care for her; what sort of a blessed, happy soul-bride is she? ||31||
Her Groom cares not for her, although she is known as a blessed and happily married wife.

(Pir) Parmeshvar does not even ask after you; such a fortunate happy wife you are! Meaning, your name is 'happy wife', but you are a deserted one. ||31|| ☬ Sri Guru Amardas Sahib, to remove the ego of both, utters:
CXEW: Agamm = beyond reach. Athaah = deep, unfathomable.
O Nanak! The happy (soul-)bride is the one who is pleasing to that carefree Prabhu,
In her father-in-law's home hereafter, and in her parents' home in this world, she belongs to her Husband Lord. Her Husband is Inaccessible and Unfathomable.
Here and hereafter, the bride belongs to her Groom; the Groom who is Unapproachable and Unfathomable.
Vahiguru, (agamm) unfathomable by mind and speech, is the Husband of all; (saahurai peeeeai) in this world and the next, the soul-bride belongs to that Husband.
BU38: Beparvaah bhaavai = is pleasing to the Carefree One. ||32||

who stays His, in this world and the next. The Husband, Parmatma, is beyond the reach of beings, and very deep (that is, He is so large-hearted that He is not angered even by those who go astray). ||32||
O Nanak, she is the happy soul-bride, who is pleasing to her Carefree Lord. ||32||
Nanak, she alone is the happy bride, who is pleasing to her care-free Lord.

Sri Guru ji says: but those who are pleasing to that carefree Hari — such saintly happy wives are blessed. ||32|| ☬ Once Sri Farid ji went to Faridkot and stayed there for some time. There was a king there named Mokalhar. Concerning his death, Sri Farid ji says:
EGM3: Sambahee = adorned, decked out. Nachind = carefree.
(The soul-bride who,) bathed and washed, got ready (hoping to meet the Husband), (but then) went to sleep without a care,
Bathing, washing and decorating herself, she comes and sleeps without anxiety.
Bathing, washing and bedecking herself, she comes and sleeps without care,
The one whose body was bathed and washed — that is, made bright — was (sambahee) adorned, that is, looked beautiful, and came and slept without a care in the palace.
S689: Berree = smeared, soiled. Kathooree = musk. Gandh = fragrance. ||33||

O Farid! Her fragrance of musk flew away; she was left full (of the smell) of asafoetida (that is, if one performs outward religious practices but misses remembrance, all good qualities go, and only faults are left in one's lap). ||33||
Fareed, she still smells like asafoetida; the fragrance of musk is gone. ||33||
and she remains smeared with asafoetida and loses the fragrance of musk. Farid!

That gross body, the (berree) vessel of asafoetida, lies here, and the subtle body, like the fragrance of (kathooree) musk, has gone. Or: one bathed at places of pilgrimage, and by doing deeds such as bathing and washing was (sambahee) adorned, and also made the mind still in nirvikalp samadhi; but even through doing these deeds the (berree) strong — that is, other — (hing) ego remained, and the devotion — the attainment of Parmeshvar — that was like the fragrance of musk went; meaning, it was not attained. ||33||
KME3: Sahu = husband. Sah preet = the husband's love. (Note: let readers carefully see the difference in spelling, pronunciation and meaning between the words 'sahu' and 'sah').
If my love for the Husband (Prabhu) does not break, then I have no fear of youth (passing) away.
I am not afraid of losing my youth, as long as I do not lose the Love of my Husband Lord.
I fear not the departure of my youth, if my Bridegroom's love departs not.
If the (sah) Husband's love does not leave my heart, then I will not fear as this youth passes.
HRNP: O Farid! So many youths, empty of love (for Prabhu), have withered and dried up (that is, if love for Prabhu's feet has not formed, the youth of human life has gone in vain). ||34||
Fareed, so many youths, without His Love, have dried up and withered away. ||34||
Farid! Myriad of youth have withered and dried up without the Lord's love.
Without love for Parmeshvar, so many of beings' youths have withered and perished; meaning, they have changed. ||34|| ☬ He makes a prayer before Sri Akal Purakh ji:
0FE3: Chint = worry. Khatola = a small cot, a little bed. Birah = separation. Birahi = (pining) in separation. Vichhaavan = mattress.
O Farid! (Forgetting the remembrance of Prabhu,) worry (has become our) little bed, pain is (that bed's) webbing, and because of separation (pain) is the mattress and the quilt.
Fareed, anxiety is my bed, pain is my mattress, and the pain of separation is my blanket and quilt.
Farid! Anxiety is my cot, affliction is my bottom and pangs of separation from God my bedding and quilt.
Sri Farid ji says: worry is our (khatola) bed, and it is woven with the webbing of pain; separation from You — or love for You — is made the mattress and the quilt.
B8XE: O true Master! See — (separated from You) this is (the state of) our life. ||35||
Behold, this is my life, O my True Lord and Master. ||35||
This is my life, see You, O my True Lord.
In this way is our life. So, O true Master, look upon us with a glance of grace. ||35||
L7JF: Birha = separation. Aakheeai = is said. Sultaan = king.
Everyone says, "(Alas!) separation (is bad), (alas!) separation (is bad)." But O separation! You are the king (that is, I salute you, because),
Many talk of the pain and suffering of separation; O pain, you are the ruler of all.
Men, talk of the Lord's love and its pangs. O the Lord's pangs you are the monarch of all.
O love! You are called 'birha'. So, O love, you are the king of all spiritual practices; meaning, you are the chief of the divine virtues.
5QQY: Jit tan = in which body. Birahu = separation, the awareness of separation. Masaan = the cremation ground. Jit = in which. Tan = in the body. ||36||

O Farid! The body in which the pang of separation does not arise (that is, the person who has never felt the sting of "I am separated from Prabhu") — know that body as a cremation ground (that is, the soul living in that body is burning in vices). ||36||
Fareed, that body, within which love of the Lord does not well up - look upon that body as a cremation ground. ||36||
Farid! The body, in which the Lord's love blossoms not, that body should be considered as the cremation ground.
For the body in which (birahu) love has not arisen — that body is impure like (masaan) a corpse, or like a cremation ground. ||36||
TLVN: E = these things of the world. Vis = poison. Khand livaarr = coated with sugar.
O Farid! These things of the world are (as it were) poisonous shoots, kept coated with sugar.
Fareed, these are poisonous sprouts coated with sugar.
Farid! These pleasures are the poisonous sprouts, coated with sugar.
Sri Farid ji says: these women are shoots of poison, wrapped (livaarr) on the outside in the sugar of clothes, ornaments and the like.
PT96: Ik = many beings. Raahede = sowing. Rah gae = grew weary, came to an end, died. Raadhee = sown. Ujaarr = laying waste, leaving without an owner. ||37||
Many died while still sowing these shoots, and left what they had sown (half-way). ||37||
Some die planting them, and some are ruined, harvesting and enjoying them. ||37||
Some die sowing sins and some are ruined, reaping and enjoying them.

Some were left in the middle — that is, while still betrothed they renounced and went away; and some, becoming detached, laid waste their wedded wives and went away; meaning, became renunciants. ||37||
NQER: Handh kai = roaming, wandering, running about. Samm = sleeping.
O Farid! (For these 'poison shoots', for these things of the world,) you have wasted the four (watches of the day) running about, and lost the four (watches of the night) sleeping.
Fareed, the hours of the day are lost wandering around, and the hours of the night are lost in sleep.
Farid! Men lose four watches of the day in wandering and the four of the night in sleep.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! You have lost the four watches — that is, the day — (handh) wandering about, and you have lost the four watches of the night sleeping.
UZVV: Mangeseea = will ask. Aanho = had come. Kerhe kamm = for what task? (under the letter 'r' there is an 'h'). ||38||
Parmatma will ask for the account: for what task had you come (into the world)? ||38||
God will call for your account, and ask you why you came into this world. ||38||
God will call for yours account and ask of you the purpose for which you come into the world?

At the time when (rab) Vahiguru will ask you for the (lekha) account, He will say: "Having done what deeds have you come?" Or: "What deeds had you come to do, and what did you do?" The meaning is: you have done no good deed at all. ||38||
Q5RC: Dar = at the door. Darvaajai = at the gateway. Jaai kai = going. Kiu = have you?
O Farid! Going to (some) door, (some) gateway, have you (ever) seen the gong (being struck)?
Fareed, you have gone to the Lord's Door. Have you seen the gong there?
Farid! Going to the door of the court, why have you not seen the gong?
Sri Farid ji says: O mind! Going (dar) inside the gateways of kings, (kiu) have you seen the gong as well?
EFLM: This (gong) is beaten though blameless; (then) what will be the state of us who are to blame? ||39||
This blameless object is being beaten - imagine what is in store for us sinners! ||39||
The sinless in being beaten, what shall be the condition of us, the sinners?
See: this gong is beaten without any fault; then what will be the state of us who have faults? The meaning is: it will surely be a bad state; so give up faults. ||39||
FX6P: Ghareee ghareee = after every ghari. Pahree = after every watch. Sajaai = punishment, beating.
(The gong) is struck after every ghari; after every watch it takes a beating.
Each and every hour, it is beaten; it is punished every day.
Every ghari, it is beaten and every watch, it receives punishment.
This gong is struck after every single ghari, and after a watch, when the full count is rung, it receives a greater punishment.
1GWR: Herra = body. Siu [sic: 'jiu'] = like. Rain = the night (of life). Vihaai = passes, goes by. ||40||
Just like the gong is that body (which has spent its life only for the sake of the 'poison shoots'); its night (of life) passes only in pain. ||40||
This beautiful body is like the gong; it passes the night in pain. ||40||
The beauteous body is like the bell and passes the night in pain.
Without the worship of Vahiguru, the (herra) body is punished like the gong; meaning, it passes the night of its lifespan in pain. ||40||

984Z: (Running and running after the 'poison shoots',) Sheikh Farid has (now) grown old; the body has begun to tremble.
Shaykh Fareed has grown old, and his body has begun to tremble.
Shaikh Farid has grown old and his body has begun to tremble.
Sheikh Farid ji says: having reached old age, this body has begun to tremble.
65JQ: Kheh = ash, dust. Hosee = will become. ||41||
Even if one were granted a hundred years of life, still (in the end) the body will become dust (and the bond with these 'poison shoots' will break). ||41||
Even if he could live for hundreds of years, his body will eventually turn to dust. ||41||
Even if he lives for hundreds of years, his body shall ultimately become dust.

Even if one were to live for hundreds of years, this body must still turn to dust. ||41|| ☬ Once, in winter, struck by the cold at night, Farid ji, knowing there was warmth in a fisherwoman's oven, slept by it. 74TY: Baar = at the door. Baar paraaiai = at another's door. Baisna = to sit. Saanee = O Master!
O Farid! O Master! Do not let me sit at another's door (for the sake of these things of the world).
Fareed begs, O Lord, do not make me sit at another's door.
My Lord, make You me not sit at another's door, begs Farid.
Sri Farid ji says: O Master! Never let me sit at another's door.
GUZM: Evai = in this way (that is, at others' doors). Sareerahu = out of the body. Jeeu = soul. ||42||
But if You are going to keep me like this (that is, if You are going to make me dependent on others), then take the soul out of my body. ||42||
If this is the way you are going to keep me, then go ahead and take the life out of my body. ||42||
If You are to keep me thiswise then, take You out the life from my body.

If You are going to keep me this way, then take the (jeeu) soul out of the body; meaning, to die is better than the pain of this dependence. 5GSX: Kandh = on the shoulder. Sir = on the head. Van = in the forest. Kaisar = king.

With an axe on his shoulder and a pitcher on his head, the blacksmith is (like) a king in the forest (for he can swing his axe at any tree he likes) (in the same way a person is a chief in the forest of the world).
With the axe on his shoulder, and a bucket on his head, the blacksmith is ready to cut down the tree.
With an axe on him shoulder and water-pot on his head, the blacksmith is ready to cut (standing on the head).
O blacksmith! On your shoulder is an axe and on your head a pitcher full of water, and you stand over the forest as its enemy.
FAS1: Hau = I. Sahu = husband. Lorree = I seek. Angiaar = charcoal. ||43||
O Farid! I am seeking my Master-Prabhu (in this forest of the world), and you (O being, like the blacksmith) are seeking charcoal (that is, the charcoal of the 'poison shoots'). ||43||

Farid! I long for my Spouse and you long for charcoal.

On your (kandh) shoulder there is a visible axe, on your head the pitcher of the Command, and you stand over the forest of the world. I (lorree) want my Husband, the Master, and you want to make my body charcoal — that is, to kill it. ||43||
PFUW: O Farid! Some people have plenty of flour (plenty of 'poison shoots', plenty of worldly things); some do not have (even as much) as the salt (put in the flour).
Fareed, some have lots of flour, while others do not even have salt.
Farid! Some have a good deal of flour and some do not have even the salt.

Sri Farid ji says: some have (agla) plenty of the flour of things, and some do not have even salt; meaning, they own nothing. Or: some have plenty of the flour of good qualities, and some do not have even a few qualities, like salt.
09J9: Agai = in the next world. Sinjaapasanhi = will be recognised. Khaasee = will eat. (Note: at the end of the letters 'nhi' there is a half letter 'h'). ||44||
(These 'poison shoots' are not the measure of a successful human life;) going ahead, it will be recognised (by deeds) who is beaten. ||44||
When they go beyond this world, it shall be seen, who will be punished. ||44||
When they both go into the yond, it shall then be known, who shall suffer the strokes?

XTJR: Paas = near (whom). Damaame = kettledrums. Chhat = canopy. Sir = on the head (see salok no. 43). Bheree = trumpets. Sado = call. Rad = the name of a metre used for praise (see Savaiye Mahle Chauthe Ke, Bhatt Nalh, verses 1 to 8 ||12||).
(What pride in these 'poison shoots'?) (Those people) near whom (kettledrums sounded), over whose heads canopies (waved), trumpets (were blown) and verses of praise (were sung) —
Drums were beaten in their honor, there were canopies above their heads, and bugles announced their coming.
They, who had drums and trumpets and umbrellas over their heads and whose praises the bards sang;
Those near whom (damaame) drums and trumpets and other instruments played, and over whose heads a canopy waved, before whom bards (sado) uttered (rad) verses of praise —
KW1R: Jeeraan = cremation ground, graveyard. Ateem = orphan. Gad thee = were mixed in. ||45||
they too at last went to sleep in the graveyards, and joined the orphans (that is, became just like orphans). ||45||
They have gone to sleep in the cemetary, buried like poor orphans. ||45||
They have gone to sleep in the cemetery and are buried like orphans.
even such people of glory have gone to sleep in the (jeeraan) burial ground, buried in graves like the (ateema) poor. ||45||
GS2P: Mandap = canopies. Maarreea = mansions with upper rooms.
O Farid! (Look at the traders in 'poison shoots'!) Even those who built houses, mansions and palaces went away (leaving them behind).
Fareed, those who built houses, mansions and lofty buildings, are also gone.
Farid! Those who built houses, mansions and lofty buildings, they have also departed.
Sri Farid ji says: the people who built single-storey houses, (mandap) mansions and all such places, and then (maarreeaan) high towers — they too have gone from this world.
KBP3: Koorra = that does not go along with one. Goree = in graves. ||46||
They made a deal that did not go along with them, and (in the end, empty-handed) went and lay in the graves. ||46||
They made false deals, and were dropped into their graves. ||46||
They transacted false business and dropped into graves.
Those people made a false deal in false things and went to the next world, and their bodies came to lie in graves. ||46||
UA61: Khinthrr = patched quilt. Mekha = stitches, tacks, pegs. Agleea = many (see salok no. 44, 'agla'). Jind = (this word always ends in (u),

O Farid! Never mind these 'poison shoots' — even this soul of one's own cannot be relied on. (A worthless patched quilt can be trusted more than this, because) the quilt has many stitches, but the soul has not a single stitch (who knows at what moment it may part from the body?)
Fareed, there are many seams on the patched coat, but there are no seams on the soul.
Farid! There are many tacks on the patched coat, but there are no tacks on the soul.
Sri Farid ji says: the visible patched cloak has (agleeaan) many stitches of thread, and the soul has no stitch at all.
DLYT: Sheikhs and others who were called great all went from here, each in their turn. ||47||
The shaykhs and their disciples have all departed, each in his own turn. ||47||
All the shaikhs and their disciples have departed, each on his own turn.
Each in their own turn the (masaaik) labourers and the (sekh) renunciants — that is, high and low — all go away. ||47||
97TD: Duhu deevee balandia = while these two lamps were still burning, (that is,) before these two eyes. Malak = the angel (of death).
O Farid! Before these two eyes (while these two lamps were still burning), the angel of death came and sat (by whatever person),
Fareed, the two lamps are lit, but death has come anyway.
Farid! While the two lamps of the eyes are alight, the death's courier comes and seats himself.
Sri Farid ji says: while the two lamps of the eyes were still (balandia) giving light, Yama, the (malak) master — or the angel — came and sat down.
6YFR: Garr = fortress (of the body). Ghat = heart, inner faculty. Leeta = took, seized. ||48||
he seized the fortress of their body, plundered the inner faculty (that is, took control of the soul), and went off, putting out the lamps (of the eyes). ||48||
It has captured the fortress of the body, and plundered the home of the heart; it extinguishes the lamps and departs. ||48||
He captures the fortress, robs if of the soul and having put out the lamps, departs.
So he seized the fortress of the body, plundered the vessel of the inner faculty, and went off putting out the lamps of the eyes; meaning, he made the eyes lose their light. ||48||
8LXA: Ji = whatever. Theea = happened, befell. Sir = on the head (see salok no. 43).
O Farid! See what happens to cotton (it is crushed in the gin), what befalls sesame (it is crushed in the press),
Fareed, look at what has happened to the cotton and the sesame seed,
Farid! See what has happened to cotton and what has befallen to the sesame's head,
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! See what happened to cotton — it suffers being crushed in the gin and the like — and what befell sesame: it is crushed in the oil-press.
FC8E: what happens to sugar cane, paper, the earthen pot and the charcoal —
the sugar cane and paper, the clay pots and the charcoal.
and what has been the state of sugar-cane, paper, earthen utensils and the charcoal?
what happens to sugar cane and to paper, and then what befell the washerman's (kunnee) pot and the charcoal: the pot is heated day and night, and the charcoal is burned a second time.
4ZCD: Sajaai = punishment. Tinaah = to them. Amal = deeds, actions. ||49||
this punishment is given to those people who do bad deeds (for the sake of these 'poison shoots') (that is, the more they do bad deeds for the sake of worldly things, the more they suffer). ||49||
This is the punishment for those who do evil deeds. ||49||
They who commit evil deeds; thiswise are they punished.
So the people who do evil deeds receive punishments of this kind. ||49||
WV5H: Kann = on the shoulder. Sooph = black robe. Gal = on the neck. Dil = in the heart.

O Farid! On (your) shoulder is a prayer mat, (you have put) a black robe around your neck, in (your) mouth there is jaggery; (but) in your heart there is a knife (that is, outwardly, to show people, you wear a fakir's garb and speak sweetly to them, but at heart you are false for the sake of the 'poison shoots'; so),
Fareed, you wear your prayer shawl on your shoulders and the robes of a Sufi; your words are sweet, but there is a dagger in your heart.
Farid! On your shoulder is the prayer-mat, on your body the devotee's garb and you speak sweetly, however, there is scalpel in your heart.

Sri Farid ji says: the one who, for show, keeps a prayer mat for namaz on his shoulder, wears a (sooph) robe around his neck, has his heart full of the (kaatee) knife of envy, and outwardly speaks sweet words from his mouth like jaggery —
GBR8: outwardly there seems to be light, (but) in the heart there is (spread) a dark night. ||50||
Outwardly, you look bright, but your heart is dark as night. ||50||
From without, you appear bright, but in your heart, is the sable night.

outwardly he looks like a person of knowledge, full of light, and in his heart is the dark night of ignorance. The meaning is: outwardly they display a garb, and inwardly they are bent on bad deeds. ||50||
MTT9: Ratee = even a little. Rat = blood. (This word is feminine, but it always keeps (u) at the end; other such words that come in these very saloks are: jind, khand, mail, laj, vis, khaak).

O Farid! If someone cuts open the body (of one dyed in God's love), not even a little blood comes out (but, O Farid, you have only kept your mind on outward things such as the prayer mat and the robe).
Fareed, not even a drop of blood would issue forth, if someone cut my body.
Farid! If any one cuts my body, not even a bit of blood would flow from it.
Sri Farid ji says: even if someone cuts open the body of the detached, not even a drop of (rat) blood comes out of their body.
RRNF: Rate = dyed. Siu = with. Tin tan = in their bodies. ||51||
Those people who are dyed with God (that is, dyed in God's love) — in their bodies there is no blood (of attachment to the 'poison shoots'). ||51||
Those bodies which are imbued with the Lord - those bodies contain no blood. ||51||
The bodies, which are imbued with God; those bodies contain no blood.
The bodies of the saints that are (rate) in love with Parmeshvar have no blood in them. ||51|| ☬ Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji removes the doubt:
SGK3: Sabho = all of it. Rat bin = without blood (words that by their form always end in (u) keep that final (u) even with a postposition; here the (u) of 'rat' stays even with the postposition 'bin'). Tann = body.

This whole body is blood (that is, there is blood throughout the body); without blood the body cannot live (then, on cutting open the body — that is, on examining the body — what blood is it that does not come out?)
This body is all blood; without blood, this body could not exist.
This body is all blood. Without blood, this body can exit not.
This body is all blood, for in the first place there is no body at all without blood and seed.
NMBB: Sah = husband. Sah rate = dyed with the husband. Tit tan = in that body. Tit = in that.

Those who are imbued with their Lord, do not have the blood of greed in their bodies.
They, who are imbued with their spouse, they have not the blood of greed in their body.
So the people who are dyed in their (sah) Master — in their subtle body, the inner faculty, there is no blood of greed.
U541: Bhai paiai = by falling into fear, by living in fear. Kheen = thin, lean. Jaai = goes away.

When the Lord's fear enters into the body it grows lean and the blood of avarice departs from within.
For when the fear of Vahiguru falls into their hearts, the visible body becomes lean, and the blood of greed goes out of their inner faculty.
ASHT: Just as metal (such as gold, put) in the fire becomes clean, in the same way the fear of Parmatma removes the filth of (a person's) evil mind.
Just as metal is purified by fire, the Fear of God removes the filthy residues of evil-mindedness.
As is the metal purified by fire, so does the Lord's fear remove the filth of evil inclinations.
Just as metals such as gold become pure in (baisantar) fire, in the same way the fear of Hari removes the filth of an evil mind.
91TK: O Nanak! Beautiful are those people who, having formed love with Parmatma, are dyed (in His love). ||52||
O Nanak, those humble beings are beautiful, who are imbued with the Lord's Love. ||52||
Nanak, beauteous are the persons, who are imbued with their God's love.
Sri Guru ji says: those who, attaching (rang) love to Hari's feet, have become (rate) full of love — those people alone have become glorious. ||52||
QF75: Sarvar = a beautiful pool (sar = pool; var = excellent). Vath = the (real) thing.
O Farid! Search for that beautiful pool from which the (real) thing (the pearl of the Name) may be found;
Fareed, seek that sacred pool, in which the genuine article is found.
Farid! Search that tank, where the 'Real' thing is to be found.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother, search out that pool which is the company of the holy, from which the thing — the jewel of the self — is gained.
L9FS: Chhaparr dhoodhai = if one searches a puddle. Chikarr = in the mud. ||53||
Nothing is found by searching puddles; (there) the hand only sinks into mud. ||53||
Why do you bother to search in the pond? Your hand will only sink into the mud. ||53||
What avails it to search in a pond? Man's hand merely sinks into the mud.
What comes of searching the puddles of worshipping other gods? Only the hand of the mind sinks into the mud of things; meaning, the jewel of the self is not gained. ||53||
11A3: Nandhee = by the young woman. Na raavio = did not enjoy. Vaddee thee = having grown old. Mueeaas = mueea su, she died.
O Farid! The young (soul-)bride who did not enjoy the (Parmatma-)Husband (that is, the being who did not remember God in youth) — when that (soul-)bride grows old and dies,
Fareed, when she is young, she does not enjoy her Husband. When she grows up, she dies.
Farid! The bride enjoys not her spouse when she is young, and as grows old dies.
Sri Farid ji says: the one who did not enjoy Parmeshvar the Husband by becoming (nandhee) low — that is, humble — died (vaddee) great, that is, full of ego.
RDYH: Dhan = bride. Gor me = in the grave. Tai = You. Sah = O Husband! Na mileeaas = she did not meet. ||54||
then (later) in the grave she pleads (that is, after death the being repents): "O (Prabhu-)Husband, I did not meet You (in time)." ||54||
Lying in the grave, the soul-bride cries, "I did not meet You, my Lord." ||54||
Lying in the grave, the bride cries, "I could met You not, O my Spouse".
That (dhan) soul-bride, lying in the grave, keeps (kookendee) crying out until the Day of Judgement: "O (sah) Master! I did not meet You; so how can I meet You now?" ||54||
3C3E: O Farid! The head has turned white, the beard has turned white, the moustache too has turned white.

Farid! The hair of head is grey, my bread is grey and my moustaches are also grey.
Sri Farid ji says: the hair of the head has turned (pale) white, the beard too has turned white, and the moustache too has turned white; meaning, old age has come.
A4G8: Re gahile = O heedless one! Baavla = crazy. Raleeaan = pleasures. ||55||
O heedless and crazy mind! Why are you (still) enjoying (the world's) pleasures? ||55||
O my thoughtless and insane mind, why are you indulging in pleasures? ||55||
O my thoughtless and insane soul, why you enjoy revelments?

O mind! Having become (gahile) heedless of Vahiguru and gone (baavre) crazy, why do you still (maanahi) enjoy the (raleeaan) delights of sense-objects? The meaning is: the time of death has come near; so worship Vahiguru. ||55||
MFDY: Dhukan = running. Ketarra = how far? Needarree = ugly sleep. Nivaar = put away.

O Farid! How far can one run on a rooftop? (that is, a run on a rooftop cannot be long; likewise, how long will you stay heedless of God? Life will end at last; so) put away this ugly sleep (of heedlessness) from (the side of) God.
